questions.skill: Two-step addition and subtraction problems
questions.stem: Mia had 45 stickers. She bought 28 more and then gave 15 to her brother. How many stickers does Mia have now?
questions.solution: First add: 45 + 28 = 73. Then subtract: 73 - 15 = 58. Mia has 58 stickers.

questions.skill: Two-step problems with multiplication
questions.stem: A box holds 6 pencils. Jon has 4 full boxes and 3 loose pencils. How many pencils does Jon have in all?
questions.solution: Four boxes hold 4 x 6 = 24 pencils. Add the 3 loose pencils: 24 + 3 = 27.

questions.skill: Two-step problems with division
questions.stem: Sam shares 36 marbles equally among 4 friends. Then he gives each friend 2 more marbles. How many marbles does each friend have now?
questions.solution: Each friend first gets 36 / 4 = 9 marbles. Then 9 + 2 = 11 marbles.

questions.skill: Interpreting remainders
questions.stem: A shop has 47 apples and packs them in bags of 6. How many full bags can it make?
questions.solution: 47 / 6 is 7 with 5 left over. Only full bags count, so the shop makes 7 full bags. The 5 extra apples do not fill another bag.

questions.skill: Interpreting remainders
questions.stem: A baker packs 38 muffins into bags of 5 muffins each. After filling as many bags as possible, how many muffins are left over?
questions.solution: 5 x 7 = 35 muffins fill 7 bags, and 5 x 8 = 40 is too many. 38 - 35 = 3 muffins are left over.

questions.skill: Checking an answer by estimation
questions.stem: Sara had 52 stickers, bought 19 more, and then gave away 28. Round each number to the nearest ten to estimate how many stickers she has now.
questions.solution: 52 rounds to 50, 19 rounds to 20, and 28 rounds to 30. Estimate: 50 + 20 - 30 = 40.

questions.skill: Two-step problems with multiplication
questions.stem: A theater has 8 rows with 12 seats in each row. There are 35 people sitting down. How many seats are empty?
questions.solution: The theater has 8 x 12 = 96 seats. Empty seats: 96 - 35 = 61.

questions.skill: Two-step problems with division
questions.stem: Ana has 14 red beads and 18 blue beads. She puts all the beads into 4 bags, with the same number of beads in each bag. How many beads are in each bag?
questions.solution: All the beads: 14 + 18 = 32. Shared among 4 bags: 32 / 4 = 8 beads in each bag.

questions.skill: Two-step addition and subtraction problems
questions.stem: A store had 120 apples. It sold 45 apples in the morning and 38 apples in the afternoon. How many apples are left?
questions.solution: Apples sold: 45 + 38 = 83. Apples left: 120 - 83 = 37.

questions.skill: Checking an answer by estimation
questions.stem: Kim has 100 dollars and buys 3 toys that cost 29 dollars each. Round the price of a toy to the nearest ten dollars to estimate how much money Kim has left.
questions.solution: 29 rounds to 30. Three toys cost about 3 x 30 = 90 dollars. About 100 - 90 = 10 dollars are left.

questions.skill: Interpreting remainders
questions.stem: Ella has 25 red beads and 18 blue beads. She makes bracelets with 8 beads each, using as many beads as she can. How many beads are left over?
questions.solution: Ella has 25 + 18 = 43 beads. 43 / 8 = 5 bracelets with 3 beads left over, since 8 x 5 = 40 and 43 - 40 = 3.

questions.skill: Two-step problems with division
questions.stem: Rosa has 33 stamps. She buys 15 more and puts all of her stamps in an album with 6 stamps on each page. How many pages does she fill?
questions.solution: Rosa has 33 + 15 = 48 stamps. Each page holds 6, so 48 / 6 = 8 pages.

questions.skill: Interpreting remainders
questions.stem: A teacher takes 29 students on a trip. Each van seats 6 students. How many vans does she need so that every student has a seat?
questions.solution: 29 / 6 = 4 with 5 students left over. Those 5 students need another van, so she needs 4 + 1 = 5 vans.

questions.skill: Two-step addition and subtraction problems
questions.stem: A parking lot has 75 cars. Then 22 cars leave and 14 cars arrive. How many cars are in the lot now?
questions.solution: 75 - 22 = 53 cars are left after some leave. Then 53 + 14 = 67 cars.

questions.skill: Two-step addition and subtraction problems
questions.stem: A library had 250 books. It got 80 new books and then lent out 120 books. How many books does the library have now?
questions.solution: First add: 250 + 80 = 330. Then subtract: 330 - 120 = 210. The library has 210 books.

questions.skill: Checking an answer by estimation
questions.stem: A farmer has 200 apples. He fills 6 baskets with 28 apples in each basket. Round 28 to the nearest ten to estimate how many apples are left.
questions.solution: 28 rounds to 30. The baskets hold about 30 x 6 = 180 apples. 200 - 180 = 20 apples are left.

questions.skill: Interpreting remainders
questions.stem: A rope is 47 feet long. Pete cuts it into pieces that are each 5 feet long. How many pieces of exactly 5 feet can he cut?
questions.solution: 47 / 5 = 9 with 2 feet left over. The leftover 2 feet is too short, so he gets 9 pieces.

questions.skill: Interpreting remainders
questions.stem: A school has 50 children for lunch. Each table seats 4 children. How many tables are needed so that every child has a seat?
questions.solution: 50 / 4 = 12 with 2 children left over. Those 2 children need a table too, so 12 + 1 = 13 tables.

questions.skill: Two-step problems with division
questions.stem: A coach has 63 water bottles to share equally among 7 teams. Each team gives 4 of its bottles to the referees. How many bottles does each team keep?
questions.solution: 63 / 7 = 9 bottles for each team. Each team gives away 4, so it keeps 9 - 4 = 5.

questions.skill: Problems that use all four operations
questions.stem: Kim reads 9 pages each day for 5 days. Her book has 60 pages. How many pages does she still have to read?
questions.solution: She has read 9 x 5 = 45 pages. 60 - 45 = 15 pages are left.

questions.skill: Two-step problems with multiplication
questions.stem: Nora practices violin for 10 minutes each day for 6 days. On the seventh day she practices for 25 minutes. How many minutes does she practice in all?
questions.solution: In 6 days she practices 10 x 6 = 60 minutes. Add the seventh day: 60 + 25 = 85 minutes.

questions.skill: Interpreting remainders
questions.stem: Max has 35 cards. He puts the same number of cards in each of 4 folders, using as many cards as he can. How many cards are in each folder?
questions.solution: 35 / 4 = 8 with 3 left over. Each folder gets 8 cards, and the 3 extra cards are not put in a folder.

solve.work: 35 ÷ 4 = 8 remainder 3, so 8 cards in each folder (3 left over).

questions.skill: Checking an answer by estimation
questions.stem: Sue has 48 shells. She finds 31 more and then 22 more. Round each number to the nearest ten to estimate how many shells she has.
questions.solution: 48 rounds to 50, 31 rounds to 30 and 22 rounds to 20. 50 + 30 + 20 = 100.

questions.skill: Checking an answer by estimation
questions.stem: Which is the best estimate of $62 + 39 + 18$ when each number is rounded to the nearest ten?
questions.solution: 62 rounds to 60, 39 rounds to 40 and 18 rounds to 20. 60 + 40 + 20 = 120.

questions.skill: Two-step problems with multiplication
questions.stem: A farmer plants 9 rows of corn with 7 plants in each row. Then 12 of the plants do not grow. How many corn plants grow?
questions.solution: 9 x 7 = 63 plants were planted. 63 - 12 = 51 plants grow.

questions.skill: Two-step problems with multiplication
questions.stem: A bakery sells 5 trays of cookies with 8 cookies on each tray. It also sells 7 single cookies. How many cookies does the bakery sell in all?
questions.solution: The trays hold 5 x 8 = 40 cookies. Add the 7 single cookies: 40 + 7 = 47.

questions.skill: Two-step problems with division
questions.stem: A scout troop picks 48 apples and shares them equally among 6 baskets. Then 5 more apples are put in each basket. How many apples are in each basket now?
questions.solution: 48 / 6 = 8 apples in each basket at first. Adding 5 more to each basket gives 8 + 5 = 13.

questions.skill: Problems that use all four operations
questions.stem: Ivy has 5 packs with 6 beads in each pack. She uses 9 beads to make a bracelet. Which expression shows how many beads she has left?
questions.solution: The packs hold 5 x 6 beads in all. She uses 9 of them, so subtract 9: $5 \times 6 - 9$ (which is 21 beads).

questions.skill: Two-step problems with division
questions.stem: Four friends share the cost of a game that costs 36 dollars and a snack that costs 12 dollars. They each pay the same amount. How many dollars does each friend pay?
questions.solution: The total cost is 36 + 12 = 48 dollars. Shared among 4 friends: 48 / 4 = 12 dollars each.

questions.skill: Problems that use all four operations
questions.stem: Ben has 3 boxes with 4 toy cars in each box. A friend gives him 8 more cars. He puts all the cars equally into 4 bags. How many cars are in each bag?
questions.solution: 3 x 4 = 12 cars in the boxes. Add 8: 12 + 8 = 20 cars. Share into 4 bags: 20 / 4 = 5 cars in each bag.

questions.skill: Two-step problems with multiplication
questions.stem: Luis buys 4 packs of juice boxes with 6 boxes in each pack. He drinks 5 of the boxes. How many juice boxes are left?
questions.solution: 4 x 6 = 24 juice boxes in all. After he drinks 5, 24 - 5 = 19 are left.

questions.skill: Two-step addition and subtraction problems
questions.stem: Dana scored 36 points in the first game and 29 points in the second game. Her goal is 80 points in all. How many more points does she need to reach her goal?
questions.solution: Points so far: 36 + 29 = 65. Points still needed: 80 - 65 = 15.

questions.skill: Two-step problems with multiplication
questions.stem: Mr. Reed has 6 boxes with 24 markers in each box. He gives 3 markers to each of his 35 students. How many markers are left?
questions.solution: All the markers: 6 x 24 = 144. Markers given out: 3 x 35 = 105. Markers left: 144 - 105 = 39.

questions.skill: Interpreting remainders
questions.stem: A farm packs eggs in cartons that hold 12 eggs each. It has 150 eggs to pack. How many cartons does it need to hold all the eggs?
questions.solution: 150 / 12 is 12 with 6 eggs left over. Those 6 eggs need one more carton, so the farm needs 12 + 1 = 13 cartons.

solve.work: 150 / 12 = 12 remainder 6; the 6 extra eggs need another carton, so 13.

questions.skill: Two-step problems with multiplication
questions.stem: Kara earns 8 dollars for each hour she works. She works 5 hours and then spends 17 dollars on lunch. How many dollars does Kara have left?
questions.solution: Kara earns 8 x 5 = 40 dollars. After lunch she has 40 - 17 = 23 dollars.

questions.skill: Interpreting remainders
questions.stem: A teacher has 75 pencils. She gives the same number of pencils to each of 8 students, as many as she can, and keeps the rest. How many pencils does she keep?
questions.solution: 75 / 8 is 9 with 3 left over: 8 x 9 = 72 and 75 - 72 = 3. She keeps 3 pencils.

questions.skill: Two-step problems with multiplication
questions.stem: Lin has 28 stickers. Maya has 3 times as many stickers as Lin, plus 5 more. How many stickers does Maya have?
questions.solution: Three times Lin's stickers: 3 x 28 = 84. Then 5 more: 84 + 5 = 89.

questions.skill: Checking an answer by estimation
questions.stem: Priya wants to estimate $612 + 389 - 198$ by rounding each number to the nearest hundred. Which is her estimate?
questions.solution: 612 rounds to 600, 389 rounds to 400, and 198 rounds to 200. Estimate: 600 + 400 - 200 = 800.

questions.skill: Two-step problems with division
questions.stem: A baker has 96 rolls to pack in boxes of 8 rolls each. She sells 5 of the boxes. How many boxes are left?
questions.solution: Boxes filled: 96 / 8 = 12. After selling 5 boxes: 12 - 5 = 7 boxes.

questions.skill: Problems that use all four operations
questions.stem: Jo buys 3 shirts that cost 12 dollars each and a hat that costs 9 dollars. She pays with a 50 dollar bill. How many dollars of change does she get?
questions.solution: Shirts: 3 x 12 = 36 dollars. Add the hat: 36 + 9 = 45 dollars. Change: 50 - 45 = 5 dollars.

questions.skill: Two-step problems with division
questions.stem: Ruth plans to read an 84-page book in 7 days, reading the same number of pages each day. She has finished 4 days of reading. How many pages does she still have to read?
questions.solution: Pages each day: 84 / 7 = 12. In 4 days she read 12 x 4 = 48 pages. Pages left: 84 - 48 = 36.

solve.work: 84 / 7 = 12 pages a day; 7 - 4 = 3 days left; 3 x 12 = 36.

questions.skill: Checking an answer by estimation
questions.stem: A class collects 28 cans each day for 9 days and then gives away 100 cans. Mia says the class has 352 cans left. Which statement shows the right use of estimation?
choices: Not reasonable: $30 \times 9 - 100$ is about 170, far from 352.
questions.answer: Not reasonable: $30 \times 9 - 100$ is about 170, far from 352.
questions.solution: Round 28 to 30. In 9 days about 30 x 9 = 270 cans are collected, and giving away 100 leaves about 170. Mia's 352 is much larger than 170, so it is not reasonable. (The exact answer is 28 x 9 - 100 = 152.)

solve.answer: Not reasonable: $30 \times 9 - 100$ is about 170, far from 352.
solve.work: Exact: 28 x 9 = 252; 252 - 100 = 152. Estimate 30 x 9 - 100 = 170, far from 352, so 352 is not reasonable. Only the first option uses the right operations and the right conclusion.

questions.skill: Two-step problems with division
questions.stem: A farmer packs 360 eggs into cartons of 12 eggs each. He sells each carton for 3 dollars. How many dollars does he get for all the cartons?
questions.solution: 360 / 12 = 30 cartons. 30 cartons at 3 dollars each is 30 x 3 = 90 dollars.

questions.skill: Two-step addition and subtraction problems
questions.stem: Marcus runs 3,400 meters on Monday and 2,850 meters on Tuesday. He wants to run 10,000 meters by the end of Wednesday. How many meters must he run on Wednesday?
questions.solution: So far he has run 3,400 + 2,850 = 6,250 meters. He still needs 10,000 - 6,250 = 3,750 meters.

questions.skill: Problems that use all four operations
questions.stem: Hana earns 12 dollars each week for 9 weeks. She spends 48 dollars and puts the rest into 3 jars, with the same amount in each jar. How many dollars are in each jar?
questions.solution: She earns 12 x 9 = 108 dollars. After spending 48, she has 108 - 48 = 60 dollars. In 3 jars: 60 / 3 = 20 dollars each.

questions.skill: Two-step addition and subtraction problems
questions.stem: Mr. Chen drove 328 miles on Friday. On Saturday he drove 57 miles fewer than on Friday. How many miles did he drive on the two days together?
questions.solution: On Saturday he drove 328 - 57 = 271 miles. Together: 328 + 271 = 599 miles.

questions.skill: Problems that use all four operations
questions.stem: A coach buys 6 sets of 15 cones and 4 sets of 10 cones. He puts all the cones into 10 equal rows. How many cones are in each row?
questions.solution: 6 x 15 = 90 cones and 4 x 10 = 40 cones, so 90 + 40 = 130 cones. In 10 equal rows: 130 / 10 = 13 cones per row.

questions.skill: Interpreting remainders
questions.stem: A store has 275 markers. It puts 6 markers in each pack and fills as many packs as it can. How many markers are left over, not in a pack?
questions.solution: 275 / 6 = 45 with a remainder, since 6 x 45 = 270. 275 - 270 = 5 markers are left over.

questions.skill: Checking an answer by estimation
questions.stem: A theater sold 412 tickets on Friday, 389 on Saturday, and 205 on Sunday. Round each number to the nearest hundred to estimate the total number of tickets sold.
questions.solution: 412 rounds to 400, 389 rounds to 400 and 205 rounds to 200. 400 + 400 + 200 = 1,000.

questions.skill: Two-step problems with division
questions.stem: A hiking club walks 126 miles in 9 days, going the same distance each day. At that pace, how many miles does the club walk in 5 days?
questions.solution: 126 / 9 = 14 miles each day. In 5 days: 14 x 5 = 70 miles.

questions.skill: Problems that use all four operations
questions.stem: Dad buys 5 packs of 12 juice boxes for a party. The 20 guests each drink 2 boxes. The boxes that are left are shared equally among 4 neighbors. How many boxes does each neighbor get?
questions.solution: He buys 5 x 12 = 60 boxes. The guests drink 20 x 2 = 40. That leaves 60 - 40 = 20 boxes. Shared among 4 neighbors: 20 / 4 = 5 each.

questions.skill: Checking an answer by estimation
questions.stem: A warehouse has 7 shelves with 312 boxes on each shelf and 195 more boxes in the back. Round each number of boxes to the nearest hundred to estimate how many boxes the warehouse has in all.
questions.solution: 312 rounds to 300 and 195 rounds to 200. 7 x 300 = 2,100, and 2,100 + 200 = 2,300 boxes.

questions.skill: Two-step problems with division
questions.stem: Zane has 72 cards and Tess has 54 cards. They put all the cards together and share them equally among 9 friends. How many cards does each friend get?
questions.solution: Together there are 72 + 54 = 126 cards. Shared among 9 friends: 126 / 9 = 14 cards each.

questions.skill: Checking an answer by estimation
questions.stem: Eva wants to estimate the cost of 7 jackets that cost 39 dollars each and a hat that costs 21 dollars. She rounds each price to the nearest ten dollars. Which expression shows her estimate?
questions.solution: 39 rounds to 40 and 21 rounds to 20. The jackets cost about 7 x 40 and the hat about 20, so the estimate is $7 \times 40 + 20$ (which is 300 dollars).

questions.skill: Interpreting remainders
questions.stem: Ms. Lopez has 130 cookies for 14 guests. Each guest gets the same number of whole cookies, and the cookies that cannot be shared evenly stay on the plate. How many cookies does each guest get?
questions.solution: 130 / 14 = 9 with 4 left over (14 x 9 = 126). Each guest gets 9 cookies, and 4 stay on the plate.

questions.skill: Two-step addition and subtraction problems
questions.stem: A school library has 1,250 books. It buys 485 new books and gives away 360 old books. How many books does the library have now?
questions.solution: 1,250 + 485 = 1,735 books after the purchase. 1,735 - 360 = 1,375 books.

questions.skill: Interpreting remainders
questions.stem: Tanya has 94 stickers. She gives 22 of them to her brother and puts the rest on pages with 7 stickers on each page. How many stickers are left over after she fills as many pages as she can?
questions.solution: She keeps 94 - 22 = 72 stickers. 72 / 7 = 10 pages, since 7 x 10 = 70. 72 - 70 = 2 stickers are left over.

questions.skill: Two-step problems with multiplication
questions.stem: A factory makes 235 toys each day for 4 days. Then it ships 600 toys. How many toys are left?
questions.solution: 235 x 4 = 940 toys made. 940 - 600 = 340 toys are left.

questions.skill: Two-step problems with multiplication
questions.stem: A concert hall has 18 rows with 25 seats in each row. Of these seats, 140 are reserved. How many seats are not reserved?
questions.solution: 18 x 25 = 450 seats in all. 450 - 140 = 310 seats are not reserved.

questions.skill: Interpreting remainders
questions.stem: A bus holds 48 students. A school trip has 250 students. What is the fewest number of buses that can carry all the students?
questions.solution: 250 / 48 = 5 with 10 students left over (48 x 5 = 240). Those 10 students need another bus, so the school needs 6 buses.

questions.skill: Two-step problems with multiplication
questions.stem: Priya buys 6 tickets that cost 14 dollars each. A coupon takes 9 dollars off the whole order. How many dollars does she pay?
questions.solution: 6 x 14 = 84 dollars for the tickets. The coupon takes off 9, so she pays 84 - 9 = 75 dollars.

questions.skill: Two-step problems with multiplication
questions.stem: Rae has 4 times as many beads as Jade. Jade has 37 beads. How many more beads does Rae have than Jade?
questions.solution: Rae has 4 x 37 = 148 beads. 148 - 37 = 111 more beads than Jade.

questions.skill: Two-step problems with division
questions.stem: A bakery makes 288 rolls and packs them in bags of 6 rolls each. It sells 31 of the bags. How many bags are left?
questions.solution: 288 / 6 = 48 bags. After selling 31, 48 - 31 = 17 bags are left.

questions.skill: Problems that use all four operations
questions.stem: Jake has 80 dollars. He buys 3 games that cost 15 dollars each. Let n be the number of dollars he has left. Which number sentence can be used to find n?
questions.solution: The 3 games cost 3 x 15 dollars. That amount is taken away from 80, so $80 - 3 \times 15 = n$ (n is 35).

solve.work: Games cost 3x15 = 45; left 80 - 45 = 35. Sentence: 80 - 3 x 15 = n.

questions.skill: Checking an answer by estimation
questions.stem: Ben buys 8 books that cost 19 dollars each and a bag that costs 31 dollars. Round each price to the nearest ten dollars to estimate how many dollars he spends.
questions.solution: 19 rounds to 20 and 31 rounds to 30. 8 x 20 = 160, and 160 + 30 = 190 dollars.

questions.skill: Two-step problems with division
questions.stem: A school orders 15 boxes with 48 pencils in each box. The pencils are shared equally among 24 classrooms. How many pencils does each classroom get?
questions.solution: Total pencils: 15 x 48 = 720. Each classroom gets 720 / 24 = 30 pencils.

questions.skill: Interpreting remainders
questions.stem: A camp has 134 children, and each cabin sleeps 8 children. Every cabin that is used needs 2 counselors. How many counselors are needed?
questions.solution: 134 / 8 is 16 with 6 left over. The 6 children need another cabin, so 17 cabins are used. Counselors: 17 x 2 = 34.

solve.work: 134 / 8 = 16 remainder 6, so 17 cabins are needed; 17 x 2 = 34 counselors.

questions.skill: Problems that use all four operations
questions.stem: Omar saves 15 dollars each week for 8 weeks. He then buys a bicycle helmet for 98 dollars and shares the money that is left equally between his 2 sisters. How many dollars does each sister get?
questions.solution: Savings: 15 x 8 = 120 dollars. After the helmet: 120 - 98 = 22 dollars. Shared between 2 sisters: 22 / 2 = 11 dollars each.

questions.skill: Checking an answer by estimation
questions.stem: A museum has 4,812 visitors on Saturday and 5,197 visitors on Sunday. Round each day to the nearest thousand to estimate the visitors in 3 weekends like this one.
questions.solution: 4,812 rounds to 5,000 and 5,197 rounds to 5,000. One weekend is about 10,000 visitors, so 3 weekends are about 3 x 10,000 = 30,000.

questions.skill: Problems that use all four operations
questions.stem: There are 4 teams of 7 students and 5 teams of 6 students. Each student gets 2 water bottles. How many water bottles are needed in all?
questions.solution: Students: 4 x 7 = 28 and 5 x 6 = 30, so 28 + 30 = 58 students. Bottles: 58 x 2 = 116.

questions.skill: Problems that use all four operations
questions.stem: Eli has 6 bags with 18 marbles in each bag. He loses 8 marbles and then shares the rest equally among 5 friends. Which number sentence gives the number of marbles each friend gets?
questions.solution: All the marbles: 6 x 18. After losing 8: 6 x 18 - 8. That number is shared among 5 friends, so the whole subtraction is divided by 5, which needs parentheses: (6 x 18 - 8) / 5 = 100 / 5 = 20.

solve.work: Total marbles 6 x 18 = 108, minus 8 lost = 100, divided by 5 = 20. That is (6 x 18 - 8) / 5. Option 3 lacks parentheses (would divide only 8 by 5).

questions.skill: Two-step problems with multiplication
questions.stem: A hall has 24 rows with 35 seats in each row. Six rows are closed. 500 people come to a show and sit in the open rows. How many open seats are still empty?
questions.solution: Open rows: 24 - 6 = 18. Open seats: 18 x 35 = 630. Empty seats: 630 - 500 = 130.

questions.skill: Interpreting remainders
questions.stem: Lily has 100 inches of ribbon. She cuts as many bows of 12 inches each as she can. How many inches of ribbon are left over?
questions.solution: 100 / 12 is 8 with 4 left over: 12 x 8 = 96 and 100 - 96 = 4. She has 4 inches of ribbon left.

solve.work: 100 / 12 = 8 remainder 4 (8 bows use 96 inches); 4 inches left.

questions.skill: Problems that use all four operations
questions.stem: A club sells 36 tickets for 5 dollars each and 24 tickets for 3 dollars each. It spends 45 dollars on prizes and shares the rest of the money equally among 3 charities. How many dollars does each charity get?
questions.solution: Money from tickets: 36 x 5 = 180 and 24 x 3 = 72, so 180 + 72 = 252 dollars. After the prizes: 252 - 45 = 207. Each charity gets 207 / 3 = 69 dollars.

questions.skill: Checking an answer by estimation
questions.stem: Mark has 3,962 stamps and buys 8 packs with 215 stamps in each pack. Which is the best estimate of how many stamps he has now?
questions.solution: 3,962 is about 4,000 and 215 is about 200. Eight packs are about 8 x 200 = 1,600 stamps. 4,000 + 1,600 = 5,600.

questions.skill: Two-step addition and subtraction problems
questions.stem: A school club collected 2,450 dollars in week one. In week two it collected 380 dollars less than in week one. The goal is 6,000 dollars. How many more dollars are needed to reach the goal?
questions.solution: Week two: 2,450 - 380 = 2,070 dollars. So far: 2,450 + 2,070 = 4,520 dollars. Still needed: 6,000 - 4,520 = 1,480 dollars.

questions.skill: Two-step problems with division
questions.stem: Sixteen students each have 18 stickers. They put all their stickers together and share them equally among 9 groups. How many stickers does each group get?
questions.solution: The students have 16 x 18 = 288 stickers. Shared among 9 groups: 288 / 9 = 32 stickers each.

questions.skill: Two-step problems with multiplication
questions.stem: A truck carries 4 crates with 125 melons in each crate and 3 crates with 250 melons in each crate. How many melons does the truck carry?
questions.solution: 4 x 125 = 500 melons and 3 x 250 = 750 melons. 500 + 750 = 1,250 melons.

questions.skill: Problems that use all four operations
questions.stem: Zoe has 6 boxes with 24 beads in each box and 4 boxes with 18 beads in each box. She uses 36 beads for a necklace and shares the rest equally among 12 friends. How many beads does each friend get?
questions.solution: 6 x 24 = 144 beads and 4 x 18 = 72 beads, so she has 144 + 72 = 216 beads. After the necklace: 216 - 36 = 180. Shared among 12 friends: 180 / 12 = 15 beads each.

questions.skill: Two-step problems with division
questions.stem: A theater sold 1,260 tickets in 7 days, the same number each day. Each ticket costs 8 dollars. How many dollars did the theater take in on one day?
questions.solution: 1,260 / 7 = 180 tickets each day. At 8 dollars each: 180 x 8 = 1,440 dollars in one day.

questions.skill: Checking an answer by estimation
questions.stem: A city park had 4,215 visitors on Monday, 2,880 on Tuesday, and 6,120 on Wednesday. Round each number to the nearest thousand to estimate the total number of visitors.

questions.skill: Two-step problems with multiplication
questions.stem: Dee has 5 times as many marbles as Eli, and Eli has 3 times as many marbles as Fay. Fay has 14 marbles. How many marbles does Dee have?
questions.solution: Eli has 3 x 14 = 42 marbles. Dee has 5 times as many as Eli: 5 x 42 = 210 marbles.

questions.skill: Two-step problems with division
questions.stem: A baker uses 4 cups of flour for each loaf. She has 2 bags with 150 cups of flour in each bag and uses all of it. She sells every loaf for 6 dollars. How many dollars does she get?
questions.solution: She has 2 x 150 = 300 cups of flour. 300 / 4 = 75 loaves. At 6 dollars each: 75 x 6 = 450 dollars.

questions.skill: Two-step problems with division
questions.stem: A farmer picks 1,248 apples and packs them equally into 8 crates. He sells 5 of the crates. How many apples are left?
questions.solution: 1,248 / 8 = 156 apples in each crate. After selling 5 crates, 3 crates are left: 3 x 156 = 468 apples.

questions.skill: Two-step problems with multiplication
questions.stem: A museum charges 12 dollars for an adult ticket and 7 dollars for a child ticket. A school group buys 15 adult tickets and 38 child tickets and pays with 500 dollars. How many dollars of change does the group get?
questions.solution: Adult tickets: 15 x 12 = 180 dollars. Child tickets: 38 x 7 = 266 dollars. Total: 180 + 266 = 446 dollars. Change: 500 - 446 = 54 dollars.

questions.skill: Two-step addition and subtraction problems
questions.stem: Hector read 1,248 pages in June, which was 375 pages more than in May. In April he read 290 fewer pages than in May. How many pages did he read in April?
questions.solution: In May he read 1,248 - 375 = 873 pages. In April he read 290 fewer: 873 - 290 = 583 pages.

questions.skill: Problems that use all four operations
questions.stem: Tess has 200 dollars. She buys 4 tickets that cost 26 dollars each. She shares the money she has left equally among 3 friends. How many dollars does each friend get?
questions.solution: The tickets cost 4 x 26 = 104 dollars. She has 200 - 104 = 96 dollars left. Shared among 3 friends: 96 / 3 = 32 dollars each.

questions.skill: Checking an answer by estimation
questions.stem: A farm packs 4,860 eggs into cartons of 12 eggs and sells each carton for 3 dollars. Round 4,860 to 4,800 to estimate how many dollars the farm gets.
questions.solution: 4,800 / 12 = 400 cartons. At 3 dollars each: 400 x 3 = 1,200 dollars.

questions.skill: Problems that use all four operations
questions.stem: Pete saves 14 dollars each week for 12 weeks. His sister saves 9 dollars each week for 16 weeks. They buy a gift for 120 dollars and share the money that is left equally between them. How many dollars does each get?
questions.solution: Pete saves 14 x 12 = 168 dollars and his sister saves 9 x 16 = 144 dollars, so 168 + 144 = 312 dollars. After the gift: 312 - 120 = 192 dollars. Each gets 192 / 2 = 96 dollars.

questions.skill: Problems that use all four operations
questions.stem: A school sells 240 pens for 2 dollars each and 150 notebooks for 3 dollars each. It paid 380 dollars for all the items and shares the profit equally among 5 clubs. How many dollars does each club get?
questions.solution: Pens: 240 x 2 = 480 dollars. Notebooks: 150 x 3 = 450 dollars. Sales: 480 + 450 = 930 dollars. Profit: 930 - 380 = 550 dollars. Each club: 550 / 5 = 110 dollars.

questions.skill: Two-step addition and subtraction problems
questions.stem: A stadium has 45,000 seats. On Saturday 28,650 people came to a game, and on Sunday 31,275 people came. How many more people came over the two days than the number of seats in the stadium?
questions.solution: Together 28,650 + 31,275 = 59,925 people came. 59,925 - 45,000 = 14,925 more people than seats.

questions.skill: Two-step problems with multiplication
questions.stem: A bakery bakes 48 trays of muffins with 15 muffins on each tray. It sells all but 120 of the muffins. How many muffins does the bakery sell?
questions.solution: 48 x 15 = 720 muffins. It sells all but 120, so 720 - 120 = 600 muffins.

questions.skill: Interpreting remainders
questions.stem: A school has 214 students going to a play. Each row seats 15 students, and the school pays 6 dollars for each row it uses. How many dollars does the school pay?
questions.solution: 214 / 15 = 14 with 4 students left over (15 x 14 = 210). Those 4 students need a row too, so 15 rows are used. 15 x 6 = 90 dollars.

solve.work: 214 ÷ 15 = 14 r 4, so 15 rows are needed; 15 × 6 = 90 dollars.

questions.skill: Problems that use all four operations
questions.stem: A club has 5 groups of 12 students and 8 groups of 9 students. All the students are put into 6 equal teams. Which expression gives the number of students on each team?
questions.solution: All the students: 5 x 12 + 8 x 9. This whole total is divided by 6, so the addition needs parentheses: $(5 \times 12 + 8 \times 9) \div 6$ (which is 22 students).

solve.work: Total = 5x12 + 8x9 = 60 + 72 = 132; divided into 6 teams: (5x12 + 8x9) / 6 = 22. Option A divides only 8x9 by order of operations.

questions.skill: Interpreting remainders
questions.stem: Ravi has 300 stickers. He puts 14 stickers on each page and fills as many pages as he can. He gives the leftover stickers to his sister, who already has 9 stickers. How many stickers does his sister have now?
questions.solution: 300 / 14 = 21 pages, since 14 x 21 = 294. The leftover is 300 - 294 = 6 stickers. His sister then has 6 + 9 = 15 stickers.

questions.skill: Interpreting remainders
questions.stem: Anna has 200 beads. She makes necklaces with 12 beads each and uses as many beads as she can. She sells each necklace for 3 dollars and sells them all. How many dollars does she get?
questions.solution: 200 / 12 = 16 with 8 beads left over (12 x 16 = 192). Only 16 whole necklaces can be made. 16 x 3 = 48 dollars.

questions.skill: Checking an answer by estimation
questions.stem: Mia has 297 stamps and buys 6 packs with 48 stamps in each pack. She says she now has 485 stamps. Which statement uses a good estimate to show her answer is too low?
choices: $300 + 6 \times 50$ is about 600, so 485 is too high.
$300 + 6 + 50$ is about 356, so 485 is too high.
$300 \times 6 + 50$ is about 1,850, so 485 is too low.
$300 + 6 \times 50$ is about 600, so 485 is too low.
questions.answer: $300 + 6 \times 50$ is about 600, so 485 is too low.
questions.solution: Round 297 to 300 and 48 to 50. The estimate is 300 + 6 x 50 = 300 + 300 = 600. Mia's answer of 485 is well below 600, so it is too low.

solve.answer: $300 + 6 \times 50$ is about 600, so 485 is too low.

questions.skill: Factor pairs and factors of a number
questions.stem: A factor pair of a number is two numbers that multiply to make it. Which two numbers are a factor pair of 12?
questions.solution: $3 \times 4 = 12$. The other pairs multiply to 10, 15 and 24.

questions.skill: Decide whether a number is a factor
questions.stem: Which number is a factor of 10?
questions.solution: $5 \times 2 = 10$, so 5 is a factor of 10. 3, 4 and 7 do not divide 10 evenly.

solve.work: 10 = 2 x 5, so 5 is a factor; 7, 4, 3 are not.

questions.skill: Multiples of a number
questions.stem: The first four multiples of 3 are 3, 6, 9 and 12. What is the next multiple of 3?
questions.solution: Multiples of 3 go up by 3 each time. 12 + 3 = 15.

questions.skill: Multiples of a number
questions.stem: Which number is a multiple of 5?
questions.solution: Multiples of 5 end in 0 or 5. 35 = $5 \times 7$. The others do not end in 0 or 5.

questions.skill: Prime and composite numbers
questions.stem: Which number is prime?
questions.solution: 7 has only two factors, 1 and 7. 4, 6 and 9 each have another factor (2, 2 or 3), so they are composite.

questions.skill: Prime and composite numbers
questions.stem: Which sentence is true?
choices: 9 is prime, because it is an odd number.
9 is prime, because its only factors are 1 and 9.
questions.solution: 9 has the factors 1, 3 and 9. A number with more than two factors is composite.

questions.skill: Factor pairs and factors of a number
questions.stem: The numbers 2 and ? are a factor pair of 18. What is the ?
questions.solution: A factor pair multiplies to 18. $2 \times 9 = 18$, so the ? is 9.

questions.skill: Count factors and factor pairs
questions.stem: How many factors does 8 have?
questions.solution: The factors of 8 are 1, 2, 4 and 8. That is 4 factors.

questions.skill: Decide whether a number is a factor
questions.stem: Is 7 a factor of 21?
questions.solution: $7 \times 3 = 21$, so 21 divides evenly by 7 and 7 is a factor of 21.

questions.skill: Reasoning about primes and factors
questions.stem: Only one of these numbers is neither prime nor composite. Which number is it?
questions.solution: 2, 3 and 5 each have exactly two factors, so they are prime. 1 has only one factor, so it is neither prime nor composite.

solve.work: 1 is neither prime nor composite; 2, 3, 5 are prime.

questions.skill: Count factors and factor pairs
questions.stem: Jo writes the factor pairs of 10: 1 and 10, then 2 and 5. How many different factors of 10 did Jo write?
questions.solution: The numbers written are 1, 10, 2 and 5. That is 4 different factors.

questions.skill: Prime and composite numbers
questions.stem: How many of the numbers 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 are prime?
questions.solution: 2, 3 and 5 are prime. 4 ($2 \times 2$) and 6 ($2 \times 3$) are composite. So 3 numbers are prime.

questions.skill: Reasoning about primes and factors
questions.stem: I am a number with exactly two factors, 1 and me. I am greater than 5 and less than 9. What number am I?
questions.solution: Check 6, 7 and 8. 6 and 8 are even and have more factors. 7 has only 1 and 7, so I am 7.

solve.work: Exactly two factors means prime; between 5 and 9: 6,7,8; only 7 is prime.

questions.skill: Decide whether a number is a factor
questions.stem: How many of the numbers 2, 3, 4 and 5 are factors of 20?
questions.solution: $20 \div 2 = 10$, $20 \div 4 = 5$ and $20 \div 5 = 4$ all come out even. $20 \div 3$ does not. So 2, 4 and 5 are factors: 3 numbers.

questions.skill: Multiples of a number
questions.stem: What is the smallest multiple of 7 that is greater than 20?
questions.solution: Count by 7s: 7, 14, 21. The first one greater than 20 is 21.

questions.skill: Prime and composite numbers
questions.stem: Ava says 11 is a prime number. Which reason supports her?
choices: It is odd and it does not end in 5.
It is greater than 10 and less than 12.
It can only be divided evenly by 1 and 11.
It has two digits that are the same.
questions.answer: It can only be divided evenly by 1 and 11.
questions.solution: A prime number has exactly two factors, 1 and itself. 11 has only 1 and 11 as factors. The other reasons say nothing about its factors.

solve.answer: It can only be divided evenly by 1 and 11.
solve.work: A prime has only 1 and itself as factors: 11 divides evenly only by 1 and 11.

questions.skill: Decide whether a number is a factor
questions.stem: Which number is NOT a factor of 16?
questions.solution: $2 \times 8 = 16$ and $4 \times 4 = 16$, so 2, 4 and 8 are factors of 16. No whole number times 6 makes 16 ($6 \times 2 = 12$, $6 \times 3 = 18$).

questions.skill: Factor pairs and factors of a number
questions.stem: 1 and 25 are one factor pair of 25. Which numbers are another factor pair of 25?
questions.solution: $5 \times 5 = 25$, so 5 and 5 are a factor pair. The other options do not multiply to 25: $5 \times 20 = 100$, $2 \times 13 = 26$, $3 \times 8 = 24$.

questions.skill: Prime and composite numbers
questions.stem: Which list has only prime numbers?
questions.solution: 2, 3 and 5 each have exactly two factors. The other lists each have a number that is not prime: 4 and 9 are composite, and 1 has only one factor.

solve.work: 2, 3, 5 all prime. 9 composite, 1 not prime, 4 composite.

questions.skill: Prime and composite numbers
questions.stem: Which number is composite?
questions.solution: $15 = 3 \times 5$, so 15 has a factor other than 1 and itself. 11, 13 and 17 are prime.

questions.skill: Multiples of a number
questions.stem: Which list shows only multiples of 4?
questions.solution: Multiples of 4 are 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, ... The list 8, 12, 20 has only multiples. Each other list has a number that is not one: 14, 6 or 10.

questions.skill: Multiples of a number
questions.stem: Which number is NOT a multiple of 3?
questions.solution: 12, 18 and 27 are in the count by 3s (..., 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 27). Counting by 3s goes 18, 21, so it skips 20.

questions.skill: Factor pairs and factors of a number
questions.stem: Which equation is true and shows a factor pair of 18?
questions.solution: Check each product: $4 \times 5 = 20$, $2 \times 8 = 16$, $3 \times 7 = 21$. Only $3 \times 6 = 18$ is true, so 3 and 6 are a factor pair of 18.

questions.skill: Multiples of a number
questions.stem: Which number is in the list of multiples of 9?
questions.solution: The multiples of 9 are 9, 18, 27, 36, ... Only 27 is in the list.

questions.skill: Reasoning about primes and factors
questions.stem: Which number is both even and prime?
questions.solution: Even numbers larger than 2 have 2 as a factor, so they have more than two factors. 2 has only the factors 1 and 2, so it is the even prime.

questions.skill: Decide whether a number is a factor
questions.stem: Which of these numbers is a factor of 24?
questions.solution: $6 \times 4 = 24$, so 6 is a factor of 24. Counting by 5s, 7s or 9s skips 24.

questions.skill: Decide whether a number is a factor
questions.stem: Which number is a factor of both 6 and 9?
questions.solution: $3 \times 2 = 6$ and $3 \times 3 = 9$, so 3 is a factor of both. 2 is not a factor of 9, 6 is not a factor of 9, and 9 is not a factor of 6.

solve.work: Factors of 6: 1,2,3,6; of 9: 1,3,9. Common among options: 3.

questions.skill: Count factors and factor pairs
questions.stem: The factors of 6 are 1, 2, 3 and 6. How many factor pairs does 6 have?
questions.solution: Match the factors in pairs: 1 and 6, then 2 and 3. That is 2 factor pairs.

questions.skill: Reasoning about primes and factors
questions.stem: Which number is a factor of every whole number?
questions.solution: Any whole number equals 1 times itself, so 1 is a factor of every whole number. 2 and 10 do not divide every number, and 0 is not a factor of anything.

solve.work: 1 divides every whole number. 0 divides none; 2 and 10 fail for odd numbers.

questions.skill: Prime and composite numbers
questions.stem: What is the smallest prime number?
questions.solution: 1 is not prime because it has only one factor. 2 has exactly two factors, 1 and 2, so 2 is the smallest prime number.

solve.work: 2 is the smallest prime (1 is not prime).

questions.skill: Factor pairs and factors of a number
questions.stem: $8 \times ? = 40$. What number is the ?
questions.solution: $8 \times 5 = 40$, so the ? is 5. Check by dividing: $40 \div 8 = 5$.

questions.skill: Factor pairs and factors of a number
questions.stem: Which list shows all the factors of 15?
questions.solution: $1 \times 15 = 15$ and $3 \times 5 = 15$, so the factors are 1, 3, 5 and 15. 10 is not a factor.

questions.skill: Factor pairs and factors of a number
questions.stem: Eva makes a rectangle with 28 tiles in 4 equal rows. How many tiles are in each row?
questions.solution: 4 rows with the same number of tiles in each: $28 \div 4 = 7$ tiles. $4 \times 7 = 28$ is a factor pair.

questions.skill: Multiples of a number
questions.stem: What is the fifth multiple of 6?
questions.solution: The multiples of 6 are 6, 12, 18, 24, 30. The fifth is 30.

questions.skill: Multiples of a number
questions.stem: Which number between 30 and 40 is a multiple of 7?
questions.solution: $7 \times 5 = 35$. The others are not on the count by 7s (28, 35, 42).

questions.skill: Prime and composite numbers
questions.stem: How many prime numbers are there between 10 and 20?
questions.solution: The primes are 11, 13, 17 and 19. 12, 14, 15, 16 and 18 are composite. So there are 4.

questions.skill: Prime and composite numbers
questions.stem: Which statement about 29 is true?
choices: 29 is prime, because its only factors are 1 and 29.
29 is composite, because it has two digits.
29 is composite, because it is an odd number.
questions.answer: 29 is prime, because its only factors are 1 and 29.
questions.solution: No whole number from 2 to 5 divides 29 evenly, so its only factors are 1 and 29. That makes it prime.

solve.answer: 29 is prime, because its only factors are 1 and 29.

questions.skill: Decide whether a number is a factor
questions.stem: What is the largest factor of 36 that is less than 36?
questions.solution: $36 = 2 \times 18$, and no larger number less than 36 divides 36 evenly, so the answer is 18.

solve.work: 36 = 2 x 18, so 18 is the largest proper factor.

questions.skill: Count factors and factor pairs
questions.stem: How many factor pairs does 20 have?
questions.solution: The factor pairs are $1 \times 20$, $2 \times 10$ and $4 \times 5$. That is 3 pairs.

questions.skill: Reasoning about primes and factors
questions.stem: Which statement is true?
choices: Every odd number greater than 1 is a prime number.
The number 1 is the smallest prime number.
Every even number is a composite number.
The number 2 is the only even prime number.
questions.answer: The number 2 is the only even prime number.
questions.solution: 2 is even and has only the factors 1 and 2. Every other even number also has 2 as a factor, so it is composite. 9 is odd but composite, and 1 is not prime.

solve.answer: The number 2 is the only even prime number.
solve.work: 2 is prime and every other even number is divisible by 2; 1 not prime; 9 odd composite; 2 even prime.

questions.skill: Multiples of a number
questions.stem: Jon counts by 5s, starting at 5 and stopping at 50. How many numbers does he say?
questions.solution: He says the multiples of 5 up to 50. $50 \div 5 = 10$ numbers.

questions.skill: Reasoning about primes and factors
questions.stem: Leo says, "Every multiple of 3 that is greater than 3 is a composite number." Which statement is correct?
choices: Leo is wrong. 9 is a multiple of 3 and it is prime.
Leo is wrong. 3 is a multiple of 3 and it is prime.
Leo is right. Such a number has 1, 3 and itself as factors.
Leo is right. Such a number has exactly two factors.
questions.answer: Leo is right. Such a number has 1, 3 and itself as factors.
questions.solution: A multiple of 3 that is greater than 3 has the factors 1, 3 and itself, which are at least three different numbers, so it is composite. 9 is not prime ($3 \times 3$), and the number 3 itself is not greater than 3.

solve.answer: Leo is right. Such a number has 1, 3 and itself as factors.
solve.work: Multiples of 3 above 3 (6, 9, 12, ...) have 1, 3 and themselves as factors, so at least three factors: composite. Leo is right; D gives the correct reason (A describes a prime; B uses 3, which is not greater than 3; 9 is not prime).

questions.skill: Decide whether a number is a factor
questions.stem: Which number is a factor of 42 but NOT a factor of 28?
questions.solution: The factors of 42 are 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 14, 21 and 42. The factors of 28 are 1, 2, 4, 7, 14 and 28. 7 and 14 are factors of both, and 4 is a factor of 28 only. So 3 is the answer.

solve.work: 3 divides 42 (14) but not 28. 7 and 14 divide both; 4 divides 28 not 42.

questions.skill: Multiples of a number
questions.stem: Pia counts by 8s, starting at 8. What is the 6th number she says?
questions.solution: She says 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48. The 6th multiple of 8 is $6 \times 8 = 48$.

questions.skill: Factor pairs and factors of a number
questions.stem: What is the greatest factor of 40 that is less than 10?
questions.solution: The factors of 40 are 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 20 and 40. The greatest one less than 10 is 8.

questions.skill: Count factors and factor pairs
questions.stem: Which number is NOT in the list of all the factors of 30?
questions.solution: $6 \times 5 = 30$, $10 \times 3 = 30$ and $15 \times 2 = 30$. 30 is not a multiple of 4 because $4 \times 7 = 28$ and $4 \times 8 = 32$.

questions.skill: Count factors and factor pairs
questions.stem: Which number has exactly three factor pairs?
questions.solution: 12 has the pairs 1 and 12, 2 and 6, 3 and 4. 13 has one pair, and 14 and 15 each have two pairs.

questions.skill: Reasoning about primes and factors
questions.stem: Two different prime numbers add up to 12. What is the larger of the two?
questions.solution: Try the primes: $5 + 7 = 12$. The pairs 2 + 10 and 3 + 9 and 11 + 1 do not use two primes. So the primes are 5 and 7, and the larger is 7.

solve.work: Pairs of primes summing to 12: 5+7 only (1 is not prime, 11+1 fails). Larger is 7.

questions.skill: Decide whether a number is a factor
questions.stem: Ravi tests the whole numbers from 1 to 10 to see which ones divide 36 evenly. How many of them divide 36 evenly?
questions.solution: Test each: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 9 divide 36 evenly. 5, 7, 8 and 10 do not. That is 6 numbers.

questions.skill: Multiples of a number
questions.stem: A number between 40 and 50 is a multiple of 11. What is the number?
questions.solution: Multiples of 11 are 11, 22, 33, 44, 55. Only 44 is between 40 and 50.

questions.skill: Factor pairs and factors of a number
questions.stem: A rectangle has an area of 42 square units and a length of 6 units. What is its width, in units?
questions.solution: The length and width are a factor pair of 42. Since $6 \times 7 = 42$, the width is 7 units.

questions.skill: Reasoning about primes and factors
questions.stem: Which number is a multiple of 6 and also a factor of 24?
questions.solution: 6 is a multiple of 6 ($6 \times 1$) and a factor of 24 ($6 \times 4$). 8 and 9 are not multiples of 6, and 18 is not a factor of 24.

solve.work: Multiples of 6 among options: 6, 18. Factors of 24: 8, 6. Only 6.

questions.skill: Count factors and factor pairs
questions.stem: Zoe lists every number that divides 28 evenly. How many numbers are on her list?
questions.solution: The numbers that divide 28 evenly are its factors: 1, 2, 4, 7, 14 and 28. That is 6 numbers.

questions.skill: Prime and composite numbers
questions.stem: Which number is composite and is also a multiple of 5?
questions.solution: $35 = 5 \times 7$ is composite and a multiple of 5. 5 is a multiple of 5 but it is prime. 11 and 31 are prime and are not multiples of 5.

solve.work: 35 = 5 x 7, composite and multiple of 5. 31, 11, 5 are prime.

questions.skill: Factor pairs and factors of a number
questions.stem: Which list shows all the factor pairs of 18?
questions.solution: $1 \times 18 = 18$, $2 \times 9 = 18$ and $3 \times 6 = 18$. Nothing else works: 4 and 5 make 20. The other lists leave out a pair or include a wrong one.

questions.skill: Multiples of a number
questions.stem: Which number is a multiple of both 3 and 4?
questions.solution: $12 = 3 \times 4$, so 12 is a multiple of both. 8 is not a multiple of 3, 9 is not a multiple of 4, and 14 is a multiple of neither.

solve.work: 12 = 3x4 is a multiple of both. 9 not of 4; 8 not of 3; 14 neither.

questions.skill: Prime and composite numbers
questions.stem: How many prime numbers are less than 20?
questions.solution: The primes less than 20 are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17 and 19. That is 8 primes.

questions.skill: Reasoning about primes and factors
questions.stem: I am a multiple of 4 and a factor of 40. I am greater than 10 and less than 30. What number am I?
questions.solution: The factors of 40 are 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 20 and 40. Of these, only 20 is between 10 and 30, and $20 = 4 \times 5$ is a multiple of 4.

solve.work: Multiples of 4 in (10,30): 12,16,20,24,28; factors of 40 among them: 20 only.

questions.skill: Count factors and factor pairs
questions.stem: Raj finds that 1 and 30, 2 and 15, and 3 and 10 are factor pairs of 30. One factor pair is missing. What is the larger number in the missing pair?
questions.solution: The missing pair is 5 and 6, since $5 \times 6 = 30$. The larger number is 6.

solve.work: Factor pairs of 30: 1×30, 2×15, 3×10, 5×6. Missing 5 and 6; larger 6.

questions.skill: Multiples of a number
questions.stem: Players form teams of exactly 7, with no one left over. Which number of players could there be?
questions.solution: The number must be a multiple of 7. Counting by 7s gives 28, 35, 42. Only 35 is in the options.

questions.skill: Decide whether a number is a factor
questions.stem: Which statement about the factors of 40 is true?
questions.solution: $8 \times 5 = 40$ is correct. In the other statements the products are wrong: $6 \times 7 = 42$, $9 \times 4 = 36$ and $7 \times 6 = 42$.

questions.skill: Prime and composite numbers
questions.stem: Which number between 20 and 26 is prime?
questions.solution: $21 = 3 \times 7$, $22 = 2 \times 11$ and $24 = 4 \times 6$ are composite. 23 has only the factors 1 and 23, so it is prime.

questions.skill: Factor pairs and factors of a number
questions.stem: Which number has 3 and 8 as one of its factor pairs?
questions.solution: $3 \times 8 = 24$, so 3 and 8 are a factor pair of 24. 11 is $3 + 8$, and 38 and 83 just put the digits side by side.

questions.skill: Count factors and factor pairs
questions.stem: How many factors does 36 have?
questions.solution: The factor pairs are $1 \times 36$, $2 \times 18$, $3 \times 12$, $4 \times 9$ and $6 \times 6$. The factors are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. 6 is only counted once, so there are 9.

questions.skill: Factor pairs and factors of a number
questions.stem: Which list shows all the factors of 48?
questions.solution: The factor pairs are $1 \times 48$, $2 \times 24$, $3 \times 16$, $4 \times 12$ and $6 \times 8$. 18 is not a factor of 48. The other lists leave out 16 or 3.

solve.work: 48 = 1x48, 2x24, 3x16, 4x12, 6x8: 1,2,3,4,6,8,12,16,24,48. Option 1 misses 3, option 2 misses 16, option 3 adds 18.

questions.skill: Prime and composite numbers
questions.stem: Sam lists four numbers. Only one of them has just two factors, 1 and itself. Which number is it?
questions.solution: $33 = 3 \times 11$, $39 = 3 \times 13$ and $49 = 7 \times 7$. 41 has no factor except 1 and 41, so it is prime.

questions.skill: Prime and composite numbers
questions.stem: Which of these numbers is a product of two whole numbers that are both greater than 1?
questions.solution: $49 = 7 \times 7$. 31, 37 and 43 are prime, so the only way to make them is $1 \times$ the number.

questions.skill: Multiples of a number
questions.stem: What is the largest multiple of 9 that is less than 50?
questions.solution: Multiples of 9: 9, 18, 27, 36, 45, 54. The largest below 50 is 45.

questions.skill: Reasoning about primes and factors
questions.stem: Zara says, "1 is a prime number because it only has one factor." Which statement is true?
choices: Zara is wrong. A prime number has exactly two factors, and 1 has only one.
Zara is right. 1 is prime because it is the smallest number.
Zara is wrong. 1 is composite because it is an odd number.
Zara is right. A prime number has no factors except itself.
questions.answer: Zara is wrong. A prime number has exactly two factors, and 1 has only one.
questions.solution: A prime number has exactly two factors, 1 and itself. The number 1 has only one factor, so it is neither prime nor composite.

solve.answer: Zara is wrong. A prime number has exactly two factors, and 1 has only one.
solve.work: A prime has exactly two factors; 1 has one, so it is not prime.

questions.skill: Reasoning about primes and factors
questions.stem: I am a prime number between 30 and 40. The sum of my digits is 10. What number am I?
questions.solution: The primes between 30 and 40 are 31 and 37. 3 + 1 = 4 and 3 + 7 = 10, so the number is 37.

questions.skill: Decide whether a number is a factor
questions.stem: A rectangle is made with 45 tiles in equal rows. Each row has more than 5 tiles and fewer than 15 tiles. How many tiles are in each row?
questions.solution: The factors of 45 are 1, 3, 5, 9, 15 and 45. Only 9 is more than 5 and less than 15.

solve.work: Divisors of 45: 1, 3, 5, 9, 15, 45. More than 5 and fewer than 15: only 9.

questions.skill: Count factors and factor pairs
questions.stem: Which of these numbers has the most factors?

questions.skill: Prime and composite numbers
questions.stem: How many prime numbers are there between 30 and 50?
questions.solution: The primes are 31, 37, 41, 43 and 47. The other numbers from 32 to 49 each have a smaller factor.

questions.skill: Count factors and factor pairs
questions.stem: Which number has exactly four factor pairs?
questions.solution: 24 has the pairs 1 and 24, 2 and 12, 3 and 8, 4 and 6. 28, 32 and 45 each have three pairs.

questions.skill: Factor pairs and factors of a number
questions.stem: Two whole numbers multiply to 45 and add to 14. What is the larger of the two numbers?
questions.solution: The factor pairs of 45 are 1 and 45, 3 and 15, 5 and 9. The pair that adds to 14 is 5 and 9 ($5 + 9 = 14$). The larger number is 9.

questions.skill: Decide whether a number is a factor
questions.stem: How many of the factors of 50 are odd numbers?
questions.solution: The factors of 50 are 1, 2, 5, 10, 25 and 50. The odd ones are 1, 5 and 25. That is 3 numbers.

questions.skill: Count factors and factor pairs
questions.stem: Which number has an odd number of factors?
questions.solution: The factors of 25 are 1, 5 and 25, which is 3. Factors come in pairs, but 5 pairs with itself. 15 and 21 have 4 factors and 24 has 8.

questions.skill: Reasoning about primes and factors
questions.stem: A number is a factor of 45 and a multiple of 5. It is not 5 and it is not 45. What number is it?
questions.solution: The factors of 45 are 1, 3, 5, 9, 15 and 45. The multiples of 5 among them are 5, 15 and 45. Leaving out 5 and 45 gives 15.

solve.work: Factors of 45 that are multiples of 5: 5, 15, 45. Not 5 or 45: 15.

questions.skill: Prime and composite numbers
questions.stem: What is the sum of the two smallest prime numbers that are greater than 20?
questions.solution: 21 and 22 are composite, so the smallest prime greater than 20 is 23. The next prime is 29, since 24 to 28 are composite. The sum is $23 + 29 = 52$.

questions.skill: Multiples of a number
questions.stem: What is the smallest multiple of 8 that is greater than 60?
questions.solution: Count by 8s: 56, 64. 56 is less than 60, so the first multiple greater than 60 is 64.

questions.skill: Prime and composite numbers
questions.stem: What is the greatest prime number less than 50?
questions.solution: 49 is $7 \times 7$ and 48 is even, so neither is prime. 47 has only the factors 1 and 47, so it is the greatest prime less than 50.

questions.skill: Factor pairs and factors of a number
questions.stem: Which list shows all the factor pairs of 36?
questions.solution: $1 \times 36$, $2 \times 18$, $3 \times 12$, $4 \times 9$ and $6 \times 6$ all equal 36, and there are no others. Leaving out 6 and 6 or 1 and 36 misses a pair, and $4 \times 8$ is 32, not 36.

solve.work: 36 = 1x36, 2x18, 3x12, 4x9, 6x6. Only the last option lists all of them (A has 4 and 8, wrong; B misses 6x6; C misses 1x36).

questions.skill: Multiples of a number
questions.stem: How many multiples of 6 are there from 1 to 50?
questions.solution: The multiples of 6 up to 50 are 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42 and 48. That is 8 multiples.

questions.skill: Count factors and factor pairs
questions.stem: Sol writes down every factor of 48. How many numbers does he write?
questions.solution: The factors of 48 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24 and 48. That is 10 numbers.

questions.skill: Decide whether a number is a factor
questions.stem: Which number is a factor of 48 but is NOT a factor of 36?
questions.solution: The factors of 48 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24 and 48. The factors of 36 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18 and 36. 12 and 6 are factors of both, and 18 is a factor of 36 only. So 8 is the answer.

questions.skill: Reasoning about primes and factors
questions.stem: Two prime numbers multiply to make 35. What is their sum?
questions.solution: The factor pairs of 35 are 1 and 35, 5 and 7. Only 5 and 7 are both prime. Their sum is $5 + 7 = 12$.

questions.skill: Multiples of a number
questions.stem: Which list shows the first four multiples of 12?
questions.solution: Multiples of 12 are found by adding 12 each time: 12, 24, 36, 48. Adding 10 each time or doubling each time gives other lists.

questions.skill: Count factors and factor pairs
questions.stem: How many of the whole numbers from 1 to 12 have exactly four factors?
questions.solution: The numbers 6 (1, 2, 3, 6), 8 (1, 2, 4, 8) and 10 (1, 2, 5, 10) have four factors. The others have 1, 2, 3 or 6 factors. So 3 numbers.

solve.work: Exactly four factors: 6 (1,2,3,6), 8 (1,2,4,8), 10 (1,2,5,10). 12 has six; primes have two; 1, 4, 9 have 1 or 3. Count 3.

questions.skill: Reasoning about primes and factors
questions.stem: Which statement about prime and composite numbers is true?
choices: The sum of two prime numbers is always a prime number.
Every multiple of a prime number is a composite number.
The product of two prime numbers is always a composite number.
Every factor of a composite number is a composite number.
questions.answer: The product of two prime numbers is always a composite number.
questions.solution: A product of two primes has the factors 1, both primes and itself, so it has more than two factors and is composite. $3 + 5 = 8$ is not prime. A prime is a multiple of itself, and 1 and 2 are factors of 4 and are not composite.

solve.answer: The product of two prime numbers is always a composite number.
solve.work: p x q has factors 1, p, q, pq so composite: true. Others false: p itself is a multiple of p and prime; 3+5=8; 1 is a factor of every composite.

questions.skill: Reasoning about primes and factors
questions.stem: I am a two-digit number less than 50. I am a multiple of 5 and also a multiple of 9. What number am I?
questions.solution: A multiple of both 5 and 9 is a multiple of 45. The only one that has two digits and is less than 50 is 45.

solve.work: Multiples of both 5 and 9 are multiples of 45; the only two-digit one under 50 is 45.

questions.skill: Decide whether a number is a factor
questions.stem: What is the sum of the factors of 12 that are less than 12?
questions.solution: The factors of 12 less than 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6. Their sum is $1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 6 = 16$.

questions.skill: Reasoning about primes and factors
questions.stem: Nia says, "Any number that ends in 3 is prime." Which number shows that Nia is wrong?
questions.solution: $33 = 3 \times 11$, so it is composite even though it ends in 3. 13, 23 and 43 are prime, so they do not show Nia is wrong.

solve.work: 33 = 3×11 is composite and ends in 3; 13, 43, 23 are prime.

questions.skill: Factor pairs and factors of a number
questions.stem: A rectangle has an area of 48 square centimeters. Its length is 3 times its width, and both are whole numbers. What is the width, in centimeters?
questions.solution: List the factor pairs of 48: 1 and 48, 2 and 24, 3 and 16, 4 and 12, 6 and 8. Only 4 and 12 have one number 3 times the other. So the width is 4 centimeters.

solve.work: w × 3w = 48 -> factor pairs of 48 with one 3 times other: 4×12. Width 4.

questions.skill: Count factors and factor pairs
questions.stem: I am a number with exactly three factors. I am greater than 10 and less than 30. What number am I?
questions.solution: A number with exactly three factors is a prime times itself. 25 has the factors 1, 5 and 25. 4 and 9 are too small and 49 is too big.

solve.work: Exactly three factors means square of a prime: 4, 9, 25, 49. In (10,30): 25 (1,5,25).

questions.skill: Prime and composite numbers
questions.stem: Which two numbers are both prime and exactly 2 apart?
questions.solution: 11 and 13 are both prime and $13 - 11 = 2$. In 9 and 11, 9 is composite. 13 and 17 are 4 apart. In 15 and 17, 15 is composite.

solve.work: 11,13 both prime, differ by 2. 15 and 9 composite; 13,17 differ by 4.

questions.skill: Prime and composite numbers
questions.stem: Which number is the product of two different prime numbers?
questions.solution: $35 = 5 \times 7$, and 5 and 7 are different primes. 31 is itself prime, $49 = 7 \times 7$ uses the same prime twice, and $32 = 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2$.

questions.skill: Continue a pattern from its rule
questions.stem: A pattern starts at 5. The rule is add 3. The first numbers are 5, 8, 11, 14. What is the next number?
questions.solution: Add 3 to the last number: $14 + 3 = 17$.

questions.skill: Find the rule of a pattern
questions.stem: Look at the pattern 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. Which rule makes this pattern?
questions.solution: Each number is 2 more than the one before: $2 + 2 = 4$, $4 + 2 = 6$, and so on. The rule is add 2.

solve.work: Each term is 2 more: add 2. (x2 would give 2,4,8.)

questions.skill: Find a missing term in a pattern
questions.stem: A pattern goes 10, 20, 30, ?, 50, 60. What number does the ? stand for?
questions.solution: The pattern adds 10 each time. $30 + 10 = 40$, and $40 + 10 = 50$ fits.

questions.skill: Patterns that count down
questions.stem: A pattern starts at 30. The rule is subtract 5. The first numbers are 30, 25, 20, 15. What number comes next?
questions.solution: Subtract 5 from the last number: $15 - 5 = 10$.

questions.skill: Growing shape patterns
questions.stem: A pattern of tiles has 3 tiles in Row 1, 6 tiles in Row 2 and 9 tiles in Row 3. If the pattern keeps going, how many tiles are in Row 4?
questions.solution: Each row has 3 more tiles than the row before. Row 4 has $9 + 3 = 12$ tiles.

questions.skill: Features of a pattern (even, odd, multiples, ones digits)
questions.stem: The pattern 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 follows the rule add 2. Which statement is true about the numbers?
choices: The numbers get smaller each time
All of the numbers are odd
Every number is a multiple of 3
questions.answer: All of the numbers are odd
questions.solution: Start at 3, an odd number. Adding 2 to an odd number gives another odd number, so every number in the pattern is odd. Not every number is a multiple of 3 (5 and 7 are not).

solve.answer: All of the numbers are odd
solve.work: 3,5,7,9,11 are all odd; not even, not all multiples of 3, they grow.

questions.skill: Continue a pattern from its rule
questions.stem: A pattern starts at 1. The rule is multiply by 2. The first numbers are 1, 2, 4, 8. What is the next number?
questions.solution: Multiply the last number by 2: $8 \times 2 = 16$.

questions.skill: Find a term further along in a pattern
questions.stem: A pattern starts at 4 and the rule is add 4. The first three numbers are 4, 8, 12. What is the 5th number?
questions.solution: The pattern is 4, 8, 12, 16, 20. The 5th number is 20.

questions.skill: Repeating patterns
questions.stem: A pattern repeats these colors in order: red, blue, green, red, blue, green, red. What color comes next?
questions.solution: The colors repeat red, blue, green. The pattern has just shown red, so the next color is blue.

solve.work: Cycle red, blue, green; after red comes blue.

questions.skill: Find a term that breaks the rule
questions.stem: The rule is add 6, starting at 6. Sam wrote 6, 12, 18, 25. Which number breaks the rule?
questions.solution: Adding 6 to 18 gives 24, not 25. So 25 is the number that breaks the rule.

questions.skill: Find a term further along in a pattern
questions.stem: A pattern starts at 3 and the rule is add 7. The first numbers are 3, 10, 17, 24. What is the 8th number?
questions.solution: The 1st number is 3. To reach the 8th number we add 7 seven times: $3 + 7 \times 7 = 3 + 49 = 52$.

questions.skill: Find the rule of a pattern
questions.stem: Look at the pattern 5, 15, 45, 135. Which rule makes this pattern?
questions.solution: $5 \times 3 = 15$, $15 \times 3 = 45$ and $45 \times 3 = 135$. The numbers do not go up by the same amount each time, so the rule is multiply by 3.

questions.skill: Find a missing term in a pattern
questions.stem: The rule is subtract 4. These numbers are in the pattern: 41, 37, ?, 29, 25. What number does the ? stand for?
questions.solution: Subtract 4 from 37: $37 - 4 = 33$. Check: $33 - 4 = 29$.

questions.skill: Features of a pattern (even, odd, multiples, ones digits)
questions.stem: A pattern starts at 7 and the rule is add 5: 7, 12, 17, 22, 27, 32. What do you notice about the ones digits?
choices: They are all the same digit
They go up by 5 every time
questions.solution: The ones digits are 7, 2, 7, 2, 7, 2. They alternate between 7 and 2.

questions.skill: Growing shape patterns
questions.stem: A row of triangles is built from sticks. One triangle uses 3 sticks, 2 triangles in a row use 5 sticks and 3 triangles in a row use 7 sticks. If the pattern continues, how many sticks are used for 6 triangles?
questions.solution: Each new triangle adds 2 sticks. From 1 triangle to 6 triangles is 5 more triangles: $3 + 2 \times 5 = 13$ sticks.

questions.skill: Patterns that count down
questions.stem: A pattern starts at 100 and the rule is subtract 15. The first numbers are 100, 85, 70, 55. What is the 7th number?
questions.solution: To reach the 7th number we subtract 15 six times: $100 - 15 \times 6 = 100 - 90 = 10$.

questions.skill: Repeating patterns
questions.stem: A pattern repeats the shapes circle, square, triangle, star in that order, again and again. What is the 10th shape?
questions.solution: The shapes repeat in groups of 4. The 9th shape is a circle (it starts the third group), so the 10th shape is a square.

questions.skill: Find a term further along in a pattern
questions.stem: A pattern starts at 3 and the rule is multiply by 2: 3, 6, 12, 24. What is the 6th number?
questions.solution: Keep doubling: 3, 6, 12, 24, 48, 96. The 6th number is 96.

questions.skill: Find a term that breaks the rule
questions.stem: Mia's rule is add 25. She wrote 50, 75, 100, 135. One number breaks the rule. What should the fourth number have been?
questions.solution: Add 25 to 100: $100 + 25 = 125$. Mia wrote 135 by mistake.

questions.skill: Features of a pattern (even, odd, multiples, ones digits)
questions.stem: A pattern starts at 4 and the rule is add 4. Which of these numbers is in the pattern?
questions.solution: Every number in the pattern is a multiple of 4. $4 \times 13 = 52$. The numbers 54, 58 and 62 are not multiples of 4.

questions.skill: Find a term further along in a pattern
questions.stem: A pattern starts at 8 and the rule is add 12. What is the 10th number?
questions.solution: To reach the 10th number we add 12 nine times: $8 + 12 \times 9 = 8 + 108 = 116$.

questions.skill: Features of a pattern (even, odd, multiples, ones digits)
questions.stem: A pattern starts at 2 and the rule is add 3: 2, 5, 8, 11, 14, 17. Which statement is true?
choices: All of the numbers are odd
All of the numbers are even
Every number is a multiple of 3
questions.solution: Adding 3 changes even to odd and odd to even: 2 (even), 5 (odd), 8 (even), 11 (odd), and so on.

solve.work: 2 even, 5 odd, 8 even, 11 odd, 14 even, 17 odd: alternate. 2 is not a multiple of 3.

questions.skill: Find the rule of a pattern
questions.stem: A pattern begins 3, 12, 48, 192. What number is each term multiplied by to get the next term?
questions.solution: $3 \times 4 = 12$, $12 \times 4 = 48$ and $48 \times 4 = 192$. Each term is multiplied by 4.

questions.skill: Growing shape patterns
questions.stem: A pattern of tiles has 5 tiles in Figure 1, 9 tiles in Figure 2 and 13 tiles in Figure 3. If the pattern continues, how many tiles are in Figure 7?
questions.solution: Each figure has 4 more tiles than the one before. Figure 7 is 6 figures after Figure 1: $5 + 4 \times 6 = 29$.

questions.skill: Find a missing term in a pattern
questions.stem: The rule is add 6. The pattern is 14, ?, ?, 32. What is the sum of the two missing numbers?
questions.solution: $14 + 6 = 20$ and $20 + 6 = 26$, and $26 + 6 = 32$ fits. The missing numbers add to $20 + 26 = 46$.

questions.skill: Continue a pattern from its rule
questions.stem: A pattern starts at 2 and the rule is multiply by 3. Which list shows the first five numbers?
questions.solution: Start at 2 and multiply by 3 each time: $2 \times 3 = 6$, $6 \times 3 = 18$, $18 \times 3 = 54$, $54 \times 3 = 162$.

questions.skill: Patterns that count down
questions.stem: A pattern starts at 500 and the rule is subtract 25. What is the 7th number?
questions.solution: To reach the 7th number we subtract 25 six times: $500 - 25 \times 6 = 500 - 150 = 350$.

questions.skill: Features of a pattern (even, odd, multiples, ones digits)
questions.stem: A pattern starts at 5 and the rule is add 5: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, and so on. What digit is in the ones place of the 20th number?
questions.solution: The 20th number is $5 \times 20 = 100$. The digit in the ones place of 100 is 0. (The ones digits alternate 5, 0, 5, 0, and an even-numbered term ends in 0.)

questions.skill: Repeating patterns
questions.stem: A necklace pattern repeats this order of beads: red, red, blue. So the first six beads are red, red, blue, red, red, blue. How many blue beads are in the first 20 beads?
questions.solution: Each group of 3 beads has 1 blue bead. 20 beads is 6 full groups (18 beads) plus 2 more beads, which are both red. So there are 6 blue beads.

solve.work: Groups of 3 with one blue; 20 = 6 groups (18 beads) + red, red. 6 blue.

questions.skill: Find the rule of a pattern
questions.stem: Which start and rule make the pattern 9, 21, 33, 45?
questions.solution: The first number is 9. Each number is 12 more than the one before: $9 + 12 = 21$, $21 + 12 = 33$, $33 + 12 = 45$.

questions.skill: Each place is ten times the place to its right
questions.stem: A 3 in the tens place is worth 30. A 3 in the hundreds place is worth how much?
questions.solution: Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right. The hundreds place is to the left of the tens place, so the 3 is worth 30 x 10 = 300.

questions.skill: Name the place of a digit
questions.stem: In the number $2{,}468$, which digit is in the hundreds place?
questions.solution: The digits from the left are thousands (2), hundreds (4), tens (6) and ones (8). So the digit in the hundreds place is 4.

questions.skill: Value of a digit
questions.stem: What is the value of the digit 6 in the number $6{,}700$?
questions.solution: The 6 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 6 thousands, or 6,000.

questions.skill: Explain place-value statements
questions.stem: In a whole number, each place is worth how many times as much as the place to its right?
questions.solution: Moving one place to the left makes a digit worth 10 times as much. For example, 10 is 10 times 1, and 100 is 10 times 10.

solve.work: Each place is ten times the place to its right.

questions.skill: Multiply or divide a number by 10
questions.stem: What number is 10 times as many as 600?
questions.solution: Ten times 600 is 600 x 10 = 6,000.

questions.skill: Count in place-value units
questions.stem: Ten of one place makes one of the next place to the left. How many thousands make 10,000?
questions.solution: 10 thousands make 1 ten thousand, so 10,000 is 10 thousands.

questions.skill: Value of a digit
questions.stem: In the number $53{,}218$, what is the value of the digit 5?
questions.solution: The 5 is in the ten thousands place, so it is worth 5 ten thousands, or 50,000.

solve.work: 53,218: 5 is in the ten thousands place, value 50,000.

questions.skill: Name the place of a digit
questions.stem: Which digit is in the ten thousands place in the number $84{,}205$?
questions.solution: The places from the left are ten thousands (8), thousands (4), hundreds (2), tens (0) and ones (5). The digit in the ten thousands place is 8.

questions.skill: Build a number from its places
questions.stem: What number is made of 3 thousands, 4 hundreds, 2 tens and 5 ones?
questions.solution: 3 thousands is 3,000, 4 hundreds is 400, 2 tens is 20 and 5 ones is 5. Together: 3,425.

questions.skill: Each place is ten times the place to its right
questions.stem: Which comparison is true?
choices: The 7 in 70 is worth 10 times the 7 in 700
The 7 in 700 is worth 7 times the 7 in 70
The 7 in 700 is worth 10 times the 7 in 70
The 7 in 700 is worth 100 times the 7 in 70
questions.answer: The 7 in 700 is worth 10 times the 7 in 70

solve.answer: The 7 in 700 is worth 10 times the 7 in 70

questions.skill: Each place is ten times the place to its right
questions.stem: In the number $36{,}600$, the 6 in the thousands place is worth how many times as much as the 6 in the hundreds place?
questions.solution: The thousands place is the place just to the left of the hundreds place. So the 6 in the thousands place (6,000) is worth 10 times the 6 in the hundreds place (600).

questions.skill: Compare a digit in two places
questions.stem: In the number $75{,}351$, the 5 in the thousands place is worth how many times as much as the 5 in the tens place?
questions.solution: The 5 in the thousands place is worth 5,000 and the 5 in the tens place is worth 50. Since 5,000 / 50 = 100, it is worth 100 times as much.

questions.skill: Value of a digit

questions.solution: The 7 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 7 thousands, or 7,000.

questions.skill: Multiply or divide a number by 10
questions.stem: Which number is 10 times as much as $4{,}200$?
questions.solution: Multiplying by 10 moves each digit one place to the left: 4,200 x 10 = 42,000.

questions.skill: Multiply or divide a number by 10
questions.stem: One school has 3,500 pencils. Another school has 10 times as many pencils. How many pencils does the other school have?
questions.solution: Ten times as many means multiply by 10. 3,500 x 10 = 35,000.

questions.skill: Explain place-value statements
questions.stem: Which statement about the number $22{,}222$ is true?
choices: The 2 in the hundreds place is worth 10 times the 2 in the thousands place
The 2 in the thousands place is worth 10 times the 2 in the hundreds place
The 2 in the tens place is worth 10 times the 2 in the hundreds place
The 2 in the ten thousands place is worth 10 times the 2 in the hundreds place
questions.answer: The 2 in the thousands place is worth 10 times the 2 in the hundreds place
questions.solution: Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right. So the 2 in the thousands place (2,000) is 10 times the 2 in the hundreds place (200). The ten thousands 2 (20,000) is 100 times the hundreds 2.

solve.answer: The 2 in the thousands place is worth 10 times the 2 in the hundreds place

questions.skill: Count in place-value units

questions.solution: There are 10 hundreds in each thousand. 5 thousands is 5 x 10 = 50 hundreds, so 5,000 is 50 hundreds.

questions.skill: Value of a digit

questions.solution: A digit is worth 10 times what it is worth in the place to its right. The 6 in 6,000 is worth 10 times a 6 in the hundreds place (600).

questions.solution: Dana's number is 10 times Ben's, so Ben's number is 48,000 / 10 = 4,800.

questions.solution: Dividing by 10 undoes multiplying by 10, so the number is 2,530 x 10 = 25,300.

questions.skill: Compare a digit in two places
questions.stem: In the number $70{,}070$, the left 7 is worth how many times as much as the right 7?
questions.solution: The left 7 is in the ten thousands place and is worth 70,000. The right 7 is in the tens place and is worth 70. 70,000 / 70 = 1,000.

questions.solution: The first part, 48, is forty-eight thousand. The rest, 715, is seven hundred fifteen.
