questions.solution: Write them all in centimeters. 2 meters is 200 centimeters. 195 centimeters stays 195. 1 meter 90 centimeters is 190 centimeters. 2050 millimeters is 205 centimeters, which is the greatest.

questions.skill: One-step metric capacity problem
questions.stem: A bottle holds 250 milliliters of juice. Lena has 4 of these bottles. How many milliliters of juice do they hold in all?
questions.solution: Multiply the amount in one bottle by the number of bottles: $4 \times 250 = 1000$ milliliters.

questions.skill: Relative sizes of metric units
questions.stem: A kilometer is 1,000 times as long as which unit?
questions.solution: 1 kilometer is 1,000 meters. So a kilometer is 1,000 times as long as a meter.

questions.skill: Convert metric capacity to a smaller unit
questions.stem: A tank holds 4 liters 300 milliliters of water. How many milliliters of water is that?
questions.solution: 4 liters is $4 \times 1000 = 4000$ milliliters. Add the other 300 milliliters: $4000 + 300 = 4300$ milliliters.

questions.skill: Estimate a metric measure
questions.stem: Which is the best estimate for the capacity of a glass of juice?
questions.solution: A glass holds about a quarter of a liter, which is 250 milliliters. 25 or 250 liters would be a whole barrel, and 2 milliliters is less than a teaspoon.

questions.skill: One-step metric length problem
questions.stem: A ribbon is 90 centimeters long. Sara cuts off 35 centimeters. How many centimeters of ribbon are left?
questions.solution: Subtract the piece that was cut off: $90 - 35 = 55$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Equal measures in different units
questions.stem: Which pair of measurements is equal?
questions.solution: 1 meter is 100 centimeters, so 6 meters is 600 centimeters. The others are not equal: 6 kilometers is 6,000 meters, and 6 centimeters is 60 millimeters.

questions.skill: One-step metric capacity problem
questions.stem: A tank holds 40 liters of water. Mr. Lee uses 15 liters of it. How many liters of water are left?
questions.solution: Subtract: $40 - 15 = 25$ liters.

questions.skill: Compare metric masses in different units
questions.stem: Which comparison is true?
questions.solution: 2 kilograms is 2000 grams, and 2000 is more than 1500, so the first is true. 3 kilograms is 3000 grams, which is more than 2500. 1 kilogram is 1000 grams, not 100. 4000 grams is more than 3 kilograms.

questions.skill: Convert metric mass to a smaller unit
questions.stem: A package has a mass of 5 kilograms 60 grams. What is its mass in grams?
questions.solution: 5 kilograms is $5 \times 1000 = 5000$ grams. Add the 60 grams: $5000 + 60 = 5060$ grams.

questions.skill: Order metric lengths in different units
questions.stem: Which list shows these lengths in order from shortest to longest?
questions.solution: Write each in centimeters: 250 centimeters stays 250. 3 meters is 300 centimeters. 3200 millimeters is 320 centimeters. From shortest to longest: 250, 300, 320.

questions.skill: One-step metric capacity problem
questions.stem: A carton holds 1 liter of milk. Ben pours out 350 milliliters. How many milliliters of milk are left in the carton?
questions.solution: 1 liter is 1,000 milliliters. Subtract what was poured out: $1000 - 350 = 650$ milliliters.

questions.skill: Find a mistake in a conversion
questions.stem: Dan says that 4 kilometers is 400 meters. What is his mistake?
choices: There is no mistake; 4 kilometers is 400 meters
questions.solution: Dan used 100 meters for each kilometer. A kilometer is 1,000 meters, so 4 kilometers is 4,000 meters.

solve.work: 4 km = 4000 m; he used 100 m per km.

questions.skill: Convert metric length to a smaller unit
questions.stem: A trail is 12 kilometers 40 meters long. How many meters long is the trail?
questions.solution: 12 kilometers is $12 \times 1000 = 12000$ meters. Add the other 40 meters: $12000 + 40 = 12040$ meters.

questions.skill: Estimate a metric measure
questions.stem: Which is the best estimate for the mass of a large watermelon?
questions.solution: A large watermelon is heavy, but a person can carry it: about 5 kilograms. 5 or 50 grams is the mass of a few coins, and 50 kilograms is as much as a child.

solve.work: A large watermelon is several kilograms; 5 kg best (50 kg far too heavy).

questions.skill: One-step metric capacity problem
questions.stem: Paul has 3 water bottles. Each bottle holds 750 milliliters. How many milliliters of water do the 3 bottles hold in all?
questions.solution: Multiply: $3 \times 750 = 2250$ milliliters.

questions.skill: Relative sizes of metric units
questions.stem: 1 meter is 100 centimeters, and 1 centimeter is 10 millimeters. How many millimeters are in 1 meter?
questions.solution: Each of the 100 centimeters in a meter is 10 millimeters. So 1 meter is $100 \times 10 = 1000$ millimeters.

questions.skill: One-step metric length problem
questions.stem: A hallway is 38 meters long. Jo walks along it 6 times. How many meters does Jo walk in all?
questions.solution: Multiply: $38 \times 6 = 228$ meters.

questions.skill: Compare metric capacities in different units
questions.stem: Which of these amounts is the greatest?
questions.solution: Write each in milliliters. 3 liters is 3000. 2900 stays 2900. 3 liters 100 milliliters is 3100. 3500 milliliters is the greatest.

questions.skill: Meters to centimeters
questions.stem: A ribbon is 5 meters long. How many centimeters long is it?
questions.solution: There are 100 centimeters in 1 meter. So 5 meters is $5 \times 100 = 500$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Kilometers to meters
questions.stem: A trail is 3 kilometers long. How many meters long is it?
questions.solution: There are 1,000 meters in 1 kilometer. So 3 kilometers is $3 \times 1{,}000 = 3{,}000$ meters.

questions.skill: Kilograms to grams
questions.stem: A bag of apples has a mass of 4 kilograms. How many grams is that?
questions.solution: There are 1,000 grams in 1 kilogram, so 4 kilograms is $4 \times 1{,}000 = 4{,}000$ grams.

questions.skill: Liters to milliliters
questions.stem: A tank holds 2 liters of water. How many milliliters is that?
questions.solution: There are 1,000 milliliters in 1 liter, so 2 liters is $2 \times 1{,}000 = 2{,}000$ milliliters.

questions.skill: Meters to centimeters
questions.stem: A rope is 8 meters long. What is its length in centimeters?
questions.solution: 1 meter is 100 centimeters, so 8 meters is $8 \times 100 = 800$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Liters to milliliters
questions.stem: A bottle holds 6 liters of juice. How many milliliters of juice is that?
questions.solution: 1 liter is 1,000 milliliters, so 6 liters is $6 \times 1{,}000 = 6{,}000$ milliliters.

questions.skill: Conversion tables and length models
questions.stem: A table shows meters and centimeters. 1 meter goes with 100 centimeters, 2 meters with 200 centimeters and 3 meters with 300 centimeters. How many centimeters go with 7 meters?
questions.solution: Each meter adds 100 centimeters to the table, so 7 meters goes with $7 \times 100 = 700$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Centimeters to millimeters
questions.stem: A strip of paper is 9 centimeters long. How many millimeters long is it?
questions.solution: There are 10 millimeters in 1 centimeter. So 9 centimeters is $9 \times 10 = 90$ millimeters.

questions.skill: Centimeters to millimeters
questions.stem: A pencil is 15 centimeters long. How many millimeters long is it?
questions.solution: 1 centimeter is 10 millimeters, so 15 centimeters is $15 \times 10 = 150$ millimeters.

questions.skill: Kilograms to grams
questions.stem: A bag of rice has a mass of 7 kilograms. How many grams is that?
questions.solution: 1 kilogram is 1,000 grams, so 7 kilograms is $7 \times 1{,}000 = 7{,}000$ grams.

questions.skill: Meters to centimeters
questions.stem: A hallway is 25 meters long. How many centimeters long is the hallway?
questions.solution: Multiply by 100 centimeters per meter: $25 \times 100 = 2{,}500$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Kilometers to meters
questions.stem: A bike race is 12 kilometers long. How many meters long is the race?
questions.solution: Multiply by 1,000 meters per kilometer: $12 \times 1{,}000 = 12{,}000$ meters.

questions.skill: Mixed units to the smaller unit
questions.stem: A board is 3 meters 40 centimeters long. How many centimeters long is the board?
questions.solution: 3 meters is 300 centimeters. Add the other 40 centimeters: $300 + 40 = 340$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Mixed units to the smaller unit
questions.stem: A path is 5 kilometers 200 meters long. How many meters long is the path?
questions.solution: 5 kilometers is $5 \times 1{,}000 = 5{,}000$ meters. Add 200 meters: $5{,}000 + 200 = 5{,}200$ meters.

questions.skill: Using converted measurements to solve a problem
questions.stem: Which is longer, a rope that is 4 meters long or a rope that is 350 centimeters long?
choices: The 350 centimeter rope, because 350 is greater than 4
The 350 centimeter rope, because 4 meters is only 40 centimeters
The 4 meter rope, because 4 meters is 400 centimeters
questions.answer: The 4 meter rope, because 4 meters is 400 centimeters
questions.solution: 4 meters is $4 \times 100 = 400$ centimeters. Since 400 is more than 350, the 4 meter rope is longer.

solve.answer: The 4 meter rope, because 4 meters is 400 centimeters

questions.skill: Conversion tables and length models
questions.stem: A table shows kilograms and grams: 2 kilograms goes with 2,000 grams, 5 kilograms with 5,000 grams and 8 kilograms with 8,000 grams. Following the same pattern, how many grams go with 6 kilograms?
questions.solution: Each kilogram goes with 1,000 grams, so 6 kilograms goes with $6 \times 1{,}000 = 6{,}000$ grams.

questions.skill: Conversion tables and length models
questions.stem: Zoe lays 4 meter sticks end to end in a straight line, with no gaps. How many centimeters long is the line of sticks?
questions.solution: Each meter stick is 100 centimeters long. Four of them make $4 \times 100 = 400$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Mixed units to the smaller unit
questions.stem: A pitcher holds 2 liters 300 milliliters of water. How many milliliters is that?
questions.solution: 2 liters is 2,000 milliliters. Add 300 more milliliters: $2{,}000 + 300 = 2{,}300$ milliliters.

questions.skill: Centimeters to millimeters
questions.stem: A ruler is 30 centimeters long. How many millimeters long is the ruler?
questions.solution: 1 centimeter is 10 millimeters, so 30 centimeters is $30 \times 10 = 300$ millimeters.

questions.skill: Kilometers to meters
questions.stem: Which statement is true?
questions.solution: 1 kilometer is 1,000 meters, so 5 kilometers is 5,000 meters. The others use the wrong number: 5 meters is 500 centimeters and 5 kilograms is 5,000 grams.

solve.work: 5 m=500 cm (false); 5 km=5,000 m (true); 5 kg=5,000 g (false); 5 km=5,000 m not 500 (false).

questions.skill: Meters to centimeters
questions.stem: A sidewalk is 45 meters long. How many centimeters long is it?
questions.solution: Multiply by 100: $45 \times 100 = 4{,}500$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Mixed units to the smaller unit
questions.stem: A bag of potatoes has a mass of 12 kilograms 40 grams. How many grams is that?
questions.solution: 12 kilograms is $12 \times 1{,}000 = 12{,}000$ grams. Adding 40 grams gives $12{,}000 + 40 = 12{,}040$ grams.

questions.skill: Using converted measurements to solve a problem
questions.stem: Ana walked 3 kilometers in the morning and 2,500 meters in the afternoon. How many meters did she walk in all?
questions.solution: 3 kilometers is 3,000 meters. Then $3{,}000 + 2{,}500 = 5{,}500$ meters.

questions.skill: Using converted measurements to solve a problem
questions.stem: Each of 6 bottles holds 2 liters of water. How many milliliters of water do the 6 bottles hold in all?
questions.solution: 6 bottles hold $6 \times 2 = 12$ liters. That is $12 \times 1{,}000 = 12{,}000$ milliliters.

questions.skill: Using converted measurements to solve a problem
questions.stem: Which list shows these lengths in order from shortest to longest?
questions.solution: In centimeters the lengths are 185, 190 and 200. So the order from shortest to longest is 185 cm, 1 m 90 cm, 2 m.

questions.skill: Using converted measurements to solve a problem
questions.stem: Dee has 4 kilograms of flour. She uses 1,500 grams to bake bread. How many grams of flour does she have left?
questions.solution: 4 kilograms is 4,000 grams. After using 1,500 grams she has $4{,}000 - 1{,}500 = 2{,}500$ grams left.

questions.skill: Kilometers to meters
questions.stem: Tom says that 9 kilometers is 900 meters because $9 \times 100 = 900$. What did Tom do wrong?
choices: He should have added 1,000 to 9 instead of multiplying
He should have divided 9 by 1,000 instead of multiplying
He used 100 meters for each kilometer, but 1 kilometer is 1,000 meters
questions.answer: He used 100 meters for each kilometer, but 1 kilometer is 1,000 meters
questions.solution: 1 kilometer is 1,000 meters, so 9 kilometers is $9 \times 1{,}000 = 9{,}000$ meters, not 900.

solve.answer: He used 100 meters for each kilometer, but 1 kilometer is 1,000 meters
solve.work: 1 km = 1,000 m, so 9 km = 9,000 m; Tom used 100.

questions.skill: Mixed units to the smaller unit
questions.stem: A ribbon is 3 meters 5 centimeters long. How many centimeters long is the ribbon?
questions.solution: 3 meters is 300 centimeters. Adding 5 centimeters gives $300 + 5 = 305$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Kilometers to meters
questions.stem: A bike trail is 36 kilometers long. How many meters long is the trail?
questions.solution: Multiply by 1,000 meters per kilometer: $36 \times 1{,}000 = 36{,}000$ meters.

questions.skill: Mixed units to the smaller unit
questions.stem: A scientist has 3 beakers. Each beaker holds 1 liter 250 milliliters of water. How many milliliters of water are in the 3 beakers together?
questions.solution: Each beaker holds $1{,}000 + 250 = 1{,}250$ milliliters. Three beakers hold $3 \times 1{,}250 = 3{,}750$ milliliters.

questions.skill: Find the end time
questions.stem: Lena starts her homework at 5:40 p.m. and works for 30 minutes. How many minutes after 6:00 p.m. does she stop?
questions.solution: 5:40 plus 20 minutes is 6:00. She has 10 more minutes to work, so she stops 10 minutes after 6:00 p.m.

questions.skill: Find the elapsed time
questions.stem: How much time passes from 2:40 p.m. to 3:05 p.m.?
questions.solution: From 2:40 to 3:00 is 20 minutes. From 3:00 to 3:05 is 5 more minutes. 20 + 5 = 25 minutes.

questions.skill: Find the elapsed time
questions.stem: Mia starts reading at 4:45 p.m. and stops at 5:10 p.m. How many minutes does she read?
questions.solution: From 4:45 to 5:00 is 15 minutes. From 5:00 to 5:10 is 10 more minutes. 15 + 10 = 25 minutes.

questions.skill: Find the start time
questions.stem: A class ends at 10:05 a.m. and lasted 45 minutes. How many minutes after 9:00 a.m. did the class start?
questions.solution: Go back 5 minutes from 10:05 to 10:00. Go back 40 more minutes to 9:20. The class started 20 minutes after 9:00 a.m.

questions.skill: Find the start time
questions.stem: A movie ends at 6:15 p.m. It lasted 30 minutes. What time did it start?
questions.solution: Go back 15 minutes from 6:15 to 6:00. Go back 15 more minutes to 5:45. The movie started at 5:45 p.m.

questions.skill: Add time intervals
questions.stem: Pia spends 30 minutes on math and 45 minutes on reading. How much time is that in all?
questions.solution: 30 + 45 = 75 minutes. 75 minutes is 1 hour and 15 minutes.

questions.skill: Subtract time intervals
questions.stem: A game lasts 1 hour. It has been going for 40 minutes. How much time is left?
questions.solution: 1 hour is 60 minutes. 60 - 40 = 20 minutes are left.

questions.skill: Find the end time
questions.stem: Practice starts at 3:50 p.m. and lasts 20 minutes. What time does practice end?
questions.solution: 3:50 plus 10 minutes is 4:00. There are 10 more minutes to add, so practice ends at 4:10 p.m.

questions.skill: Add time intervals
questions.stem: Ravi walks for 45 minutes and then rides his bike for 30 minutes. How many minutes does he spend walking and riding in all?
questions.solution: 45 + 30 = 75 minutes.

questions.skill: Find the end time
questions.stem: Soccer practice starts at 4:45 p.m. and lasts 1 hour 30 minutes. What time does practice end?
questions.solution: 4:45 plus 1 hour is 5:45. 5:45 plus 15 minutes is 6:00, and 15 more minutes is 6:15. Practice ends at 6:15 p.m.

questions.skill: Subtract time intervals
questions.stem: Sam has 1 hour 20 minutes to finish a project. He has worked for 45 minutes. How much time does he have left?
questions.solution: 1 hour 20 minutes is 80 minutes. 80 - 45 = 35 minutes.

questions.skill: Find the elapsed time
questions.stem: A play starts at 8:35 a.m. and ends at 11:10 a.m. How many minutes long is the play?
questions.solution: From 8:35 to 9:00 is 25 minutes. From 9:00 to 11:00 is 2 hours, or 120 minutes. From 11:00 to 11:10 is 10 minutes. 25 + 120 + 10 = 155 minutes.

solve.work: 8:35 to 11:35 is 180 min; back 25 min to 11:10 gives 155 min.

questions.skill: Find the start time
questions.stem: A recital ended at 7:10 p.m. and lasted 1 hour 45 minutes. How many minutes after 5:00 p.m. did it start?
questions.solution: Go back 1 hour from 7:10 to 6:10. Go back 10 more minutes to 6:00, then 35 more minutes to 5:25. It started 25 minutes after 5:00 p.m.

solve.work: 7:10 p.m. minus 1 h 45 min: 7:10 - 1:00 = 6:10; 6:10 - 45 min = 5:25 p.m. That is 25 minutes after 5:00.

questions.skill: Find the start time
questions.stem: A cake bakes for 50 minutes and comes out of the oven at 3:20 p.m. What time did it go into the oven?
questions.solution: Go back 20 minutes from 3:20 to 3:00. Go back 30 more minutes to 2:30. The cake went in at 2:30 p.m.

questions.skill: Find the elapsed time
questions.stem: A tutoring class starts at 1:50 p.m. and ends at 4:25 p.m. How long is the class?
questions.solution: From 1:50 to 2:00 is 10 minutes. From 2:00 to 4:00 is 2 hours. From 4:00 to 4:25 is 25 minutes. 10 + 25 = 35 minutes, so the class is 2 hours 35 minutes.

questions.skill: Subtract time intervals
questions.stem: A movie is 2 hours 10 minutes long. Dana has watched 1 hour 35 minutes of it. How many minutes of the movie are left?
questions.solution: 2 hours 10 minutes is 130 minutes. 1 hour 35 minutes is 95 minutes. 130 - 95 = 35 minutes.

questions.skill: Find the end time
questions.stem: A train leaves at 9:40 a.m. The ride takes 2 hours 35 minutes. How many minutes after 12:00 noon does the train arrive?
questions.solution: 9:40 plus 2 hours is 11:40. 11:40 plus 20 minutes is 12:00. The remaining 15 minutes take the train to 12:15, so it arrives 15 minutes after noon.

questions.skill: Add time intervals
questions.stem: A trip has two parts. The first part takes 2 hours 40 minutes and the second part takes 1 hour 35 minutes. How long is the whole trip?
questions.solution: Add the hours: 2 + 1 = 3 hours. Add the minutes: 40 + 35 = 75 minutes, which is 1 hour 15 minutes. 3 hours + 1 hour 15 minutes = 4 hours 15 minutes.

questions.skill: Add time intervals
questions.stem: Kai practices piano for 1 hour 25 minutes on Saturday and 55 minutes on Sunday. How many minutes does he practice in all?
questions.solution: 1 hour 25 minutes is 85 minutes. 85 + 55 = 140 minutes.

questions.skill: Subtract time intervals
questions.stem: School starts at 8:25 a.m. and ends at 3:10 p.m. Lunch and recess take 55 minutes of the day. How many minutes of class time are there?
questions.solution: From 8:25 a.m. to 2:25 p.m. is 6 hours, then 45 more minutes to 3:10 p.m., so 6 hours 45 minutes = 405 minutes. 405 - 55 = 350 minutes.

questions.skill: Subtract time intervals
questions.stem: A road trip takes 4 hours 20 minutes. The family has driven for 2 hours 45 minutes. How much longer do they have to drive?
questions.solution: 4 hours 20 minutes is 260 minutes. 2 hours 45 minutes is 165 minutes. 260 - 165 = 95 minutes, which is 1 hour 35 minutes.

questions.skill: Add time intervals
questions.stem: Ana practices on three days. She practices 45 minutes on the first day, 1 hour 10 minutes on the second day, and 50 minutes on the third day. How many minutes does she practice in all?
questions.solution: 1 hour 10 minutes is 70 minutes. 45 + 70 + 50 = 165 minutes.

questions.skill: Add time intervals
questions.stem: Leo starts a task at 4:50 p.m. He works for 40 minutes, takes a 15-minute break, and then works for 25 more minutes. What time does he finish?
questions.solution: The whole time is 40 + 15 + 25 = 80 minutes, or 1 hour 20 minutes. 4:50 plus 1 hour is 5:50. 5:50 plus 20 minutes is 6:10 p.m.

questions.skill: Find the end time
questions.stem: Jo starts getting ready to bake at 10:50 a.m. Preparing takes 35 minutes and baking takes 1 hour 40 minutes. What time is the baking finished?
questions.solution: Preparing and baking take 35 + 100 = 135 minutes, which is 2 hours 15 minutes. 10:50 plus 2 hours is 12:50. 12:50 plus 15 minutes is 1:05 p.m.

questions.skill: Find the start time
questions.stem: Zoe walks 15 minutes to a bus stop and then rides the bus for 50 minutes. She arrives at school at 8:05 a.m. What time did she leave home?
questions.solution: The whole trip takes 15 + 50 = 65 minutes. Go back 5 minutes from 8:05 to 8:00, then 60 more minutes to 7:00. She left at 7:00 a.m.

questions.skill: Subtract time intervals
questions.stem: A TV program starts at 7:35 p.m. and ends at 9:10 p.m. It has 18 minutes of ads. How many minutes of the program are not ads?
questions.solution: From 7:35 to 9:10 is 25 + 60 + 10 = 95 minutes. 95 - 18 = 77 minutes.

questions.skill: Find the elapsed time
questions.stem: Which pair of start and end times has exactly 2 hours 45 minutes between them?
questions.solution: 3:35 plus 2 hours is 5:35. 5:35 plus 25 minutes is 6:00, and 20 more minutes is 6:20. So 3:35 p.m. to 6:20 p.m. is 2 hours 45 minutes.

questions.skill: Find the end time
questions.stem: A meeting begins at 12:50 p.m. and lasts 3 hours 25 minutes. How many minutes after 4:00 p.m. does the meeting end?
questions.solution: 12:50 plus 3 hours is 3:50. 3:50 plus 10 minutes is 4:00, and 15 more minutes is 4:15. The meeting ends 15 minutes after 4:00 p.m.

questions.skill: Find the elapsed time
questions.stem: A train leaves at 11:48 a.m. and arrives at 3:17 p.m. How many minutes long is the trip?
questions.solution: From 11:48 a.m. to 12:00 noon is 12 minutes. From noon to 3:00 p.m. is 180 minutes. From 3:00 to 3:17 is 17 minutes. 12 + 180 + 17 = 209 minutes.

questions.skill: Find the area of a rectilinear figure
questions.stem: An L-shaped patio is made from two rectangles that do not overlap. One rectangle is 6 feet by 4 feet. The other is 3 feet by 2 feet. What is the area of the patio in square feet?
questions.solution: The first rectangle has area 6 x 4 = 24 square feet. The second has area 3 x 2 = 6 square feet. Add them: 24 + 6 = 30 square feet.

questions.skill: Find the area of a rectilinear figure
questions.stem: A rectangular sheet of paper is 9 cm long and 5 cm wide. A square that is 2 cm by 2 cm is cut out of one corner. What is the area of the paper that is left, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The whole sheet has area 9 x 5 = 45 square centimeters. The square cut out has area 2 x 2 = 4. What is left is 45 - 4 = 41 square centimeters.

questions.skill: Solve an area problem with a rectangle
questions.stem: A classroom floor is 8 meters long and 6 meters wide. What is the area of the floor in square meters?
questions.solution: Area of a rectangle = length x width. 8 x 6 = 48 square meters.

questions.skill: Solve an area problem with a rectangle
questions.stem: A rectangular garden has an area of 36 square feet. It is 9 feet long. How wide is it, in feet?
questions.solution: Area = length x width, so width = area / length = 36 / 9 = 4 feet.

questions.skill: Solve a perimeter problem
questions.stem: A rectangular picture frame is 12 inches long and 8 inches wide. What is the perimeter of the frame (the distance around it), in inches?
questions.solution: The perimeter is the two lengths plus the two widths: 12 + 8 + 12 + 8 = 40 inches.

questions.skill: Solve a perimeter problem
questions.stem: Each side of a square is 7 cm long. What is the perimeter of the square, in centimeters?
questions.solution: A square has 4 equal sides. 4 x 7 = 28 centimeters. (49 would be the area.)

questions.skill: Fixed area: compare rectangles with the same area
questions.stem: Which rectangle has an area of 18 square units?
questions.solution: 2 x 9 = 18. The others have areas 81, 15 and 20.

questions.skill: Fixed area: compare rectangles with the same area
questions.stem: Rectangle A is 2 feet by 12 feet. Rectangle B is 3 feet long and has the same area as Rectangle A. How wide is Rectangle B, in feet?
questions.solution: Rectangle A has area 2 x 12 = 24 square feet. Rectangle B has the same area, so its width is 24 / 3 = 8 feet.

questions.skill: Fixed perimeter: compare rectangles with the same perimeter
questions.stem: A rectangle has a perimeter of 20 inches. Its length is 6 inches. What is its width, in inches?
questions.solution: The length and width together make half the perimeter: 20 / 2 = 10 inches. The width is 10 - 6 = 4 inches.

questions.skill: Fixed perimeter: compare rectangles with the same perimeter
questions.stem: Which rectangle has a perimeter of 14 cm?
questions.solution: For 5 by 2: 5 + 2 + 5 + 2 = 14. The others have perimeters 18, 28 and 28.

questions.skill: Find the area of a rectilinear figure
questions.stem: A rectangular lawn is 14 meters long and 9 meters wide. A rectangular pond that is 5 meters by 4 meters sits inside the lawn. What is the area of the lawn that is covered by grass, in square meters?
questions.solution: The whole lawn has area 14 x 9 = 126 square meters. The pond has area 5 x 4 = 20. Grass: 126 - 20 = 106 square meters.

questions.skill: Find the area of a rectilinear figure
questions.stem: A figure is made from three rectangles that do not overlap. They measure 7 cm by 3 cm, 5 cm by 4 cm, and 2 cm by 6 cm. What is the area of the figure in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Areas: 7 x 3 = 21, 5 x 4 = 20 and 2 x 6 = 12. Add them: 21 + 20 + 12 = 53 square centimeters.

questions.skill: Solve an area problem with a rectangle
questions.stem: A rectangular floor is 18 feet long and 15 feet wide. It is covered with square tiles that are each 1 foot by 1 foot. How many tiles are needed?
questions.solution: Each tile covers 1 square foot, so the number of tiles equals the area: 18 x 15 = 270 tiles.

questions.skill: Solve an area problem with a rectangle
questions.stem: A rectangular banner has an area of 96 square feet and is 8 feet tall. Let the ? be the width of the banner in feet. Which number sentence can be used to find the ?
questions.solution: Area = height x width, so 8 x ? = 96. The width is 96 / 8 = 12 feet.

questions.skill: Solve a perimeter problem
questions.stem: A rectangular pool is 18 meters long and 11 meters wide. A fence goes all the way around the pool. How many meters of fence are needed?
questions.solution: The fence is the perimeter: 2 x (18 + 11) = 2 x 29 = 58 meters.

questions.skill: Solve a perimeter problem
questions.stem: The perimeter of a rectangle is 34 cm. Its length is 11 cm. What is its width, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Half the perimeter is 34 / 2 = 17 cm, which is the length plus the width. The width is 17 - 11 = 6 cm.

questions.skill: Fixed area: compare rectangles with the same area
questions.stem: How many different rectangles with whole-number side lengths have an area of 12 square units? A 2 by 6 rectangle and a 6 by 2 rectangle count as the same rectangle.
questions.solution: Find the pairs of whole numbers that multiply to 12: 1 by 12, 2 by 6 and 3 by 4. That is 3 rectangles.

questions.skill: Fixed area: compare rectangles with the same area
questions.stem: Each rectangle below has whole-number sides and an area of 36 square feet. Which one has the smallest perimeter?
questions.solution: Perimeters: 6 by 6 is 24 feet, 4 by 9 is 26 feet, 3 by 12 is 30 feet and 2 by 18 is 40 feet. The smallest is 24 feet, for 6 by 6.

questions.skill: Fixed perimeter: compare rectangles with the same perimeter
questions.stem: A rectangle has a perimeter of 24 cm. Its length is 9 cm. What is its area in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Half the perimeter is 12 cm, so the width is 12 - 9 = 3 cm. The area is 9 x 3 = 27 square centimeters.

questions.skill: Fixed perimeter: compare rectangles with the same perimeter
questions.stem: Sam has 20 feet of fencing and uses all of it to make a rectangular pen with whole-number sides. Which pen gives the most room inside?
questions.solution: Every pen has a perimeter of 20 feet. Areas: 5 by 5 is 25, 4 by 6 is 24, 3 by 7 is 21 and 2 by 8 is 16 square feet. The most room is 25 square feet.

solve.work: All have perimeter 20. Areas 25, 21, 24, 16. 5x5 largest (a square is a rectangle).

questions.skill: Find the area of a rectilinear figure
questions.stem: A rectangle is 15 meters long and 10 meters wide. A smaller rectangle is cut away from one corner. The cut piece is 6 meters long and its width is half its length. What is the area of the shape that is left, in square meters?
questions.solution: The cut piece is 6 m by 3 m, so its area is 18. The big rectangle has area 15 x 10 = 150. What is left: 150 - 18 = 132 square meters.

questions.skill: Find the area of a rectilinear figure
questions.stem: A wall is 20 feet long and 9 feet high. It has a window that is 4 feet by 3 feet and a door that is 7 feet by 3 feet. The rest of the wall will be painted. How many square feet will be painted?
questions.solution: The wall has area 20 x 9 = 180. The window is 4 x 3 = 12 and the door is 7 x 3 = 21. Painted: 180 - 12 - 21 = 147 square feet.

questions.skill: Solve an area problem with a rectangle
questions.stem: A wall is 12 feet wide and 8 feet tall. It will be covered with square panels that are each 2 feet by 2 feet. How many panels are needed?
questions.solution: The wall has area 12 x 8 = 96 square feet. Each panel covers 2 x 2 = 4 square feet. 96 / 4 = 24 panels.

questions.skill: Solve an area problem with a rectangle
questions.stem: A rectangular field has an area of 360 square yards and is 24 yards long. A fence will go all the way around the field. How many yards of fence are needed?
questions.solution: The width is 360 / 24 = 15 yards. The perimeter is 2 x (24 + 15) = 2 x 39 = 78 yards.

questions.skill: Solve a perimeter problem
questions.stem: A rectangle has a perimeter of 46 inches. Its length is 5 inches more than its width. What is its width, in inches?
questions.solution: Half the perimeter is 23 inches: width + length = 23. The length is the width plus 5, so 2 widths + 5 = 23. Then 2 widths = 18 and the width is 9 inches.

questions.skill: Solve a perimeter problem
questions.stem: A yard is 30 feet long and 22 feet wide. Mr. Lee builds a fence all the way around it, except for a gate that is 4 feet wide and needs no fence. How many feet of fence does he build?
questions.solution: The distance around the yard is 2 x (30 + 22) = 104 feet. The gate takes 4 feet, so 104 - 4 = 100 feet of fence.

questions.skill: Fixed area: compare rectangles with the same area
questions.stem: Rectangle A is 4 meters wide and 18 meters long. Rectangle B has the same area as Rectangle A and is 8 meters wide. What is the perimeter of Rectangle B, in meters?
questions.solution: The area of A is 4 x 18 = 72 square meters. B is 8 meters wide, so its length is 72 / 8 = 9 meters. The perimeter of B is 2 x (8 + 9) = 34 meters.

questions.skill: Fixed area: compare rectangles with the same area
questions.stem: Rectangle A is 3 feet by 20 feet. Rectangle B is 12 feet by 5 feet. Which statement is true?
choices: Rectangle B has the smaller perimeter.
Rectangle A has the smaller perimeter.
They have the same perimeter because the areas are the same.
Rectangle A has the greater area.
questions.answer: Rectangle B has the smaller perimeter.
questions.solution: Both areas are 60 square feet. The perimeter of A is 2 x (3 + 20) = 46 feet and of B is 2 x (12 + 5) = 34 feet. So B has the smaller perimeter.

solve.answer: Rectangle B has the smaller perimeter.
solve.work: Both areas 60. Perimeters A=46, B=34. B smaller.

questions.skill: Fixed perimeter: compare rectangles with the same perimeter
questions.stem: Rectangular pens have whole-number sides (in meters) and a perimeter of 18 meters. What is the difference between the greatest possible area and the least possible area, in square meters?
questions.solution: The length and width add to 9. The pairs are 1 and 8 (area 8), 2 and 7 (14), 3 and 6 (18), and 4 and 5 (20). The greatest area is 20, the least is 8, and the difference is 12.

questions.skill: Fixed perimeter: compare rectangles with the same perimeter
questions.stem: A rectangular garden and a square garden both have a perimeter of 40 meters. The rectangular garden is 14 meters long. Which statement is true?
choices: The rectangular garden has 16 more square meters of area.
Both gardens have the same area.
The square garden has 4 more square meters of area.
The square garden has 16 more square meters of area.
questions.answer: The square garden has 16 more square meters of area.
questions.solution: The rectangle is 14 m long, so its width is 40 / 2 - 14 = 6 m and its area is 84. The square has sides of 40 / 4 = 10 m and area 100. The difference is 100 - 84 = 16 square meters.

solve.answer: The square garden has 16 more square meters of area.
solve.work: Rectangle 14 by 6 = 84; square side 10, area 100; difference 16, square larger.

questions.skill: Tell categorical from numerical data questions
questions.stem: Which question gives numerical data? (Its answers are numbers.)
choices: What is your favorite color of the rainbow?
How many brothers and sisters do you have?
Which season of the year do you like best?
Which kind of pet would you like to have?
questions.answer: How many brothers and sisters do you have?
questions.solution: A numerical question has answers that are numbers, such as 0, 1 or 2 brothers and sisters. The other three questions have answers that are names (colors, seasons, pets), so they give categorical data.

solve.answer: How many brothers and sisters do you have?
solve.work: Only the siblings question has number answers; colour, pet kind and season are categories.

questions.skill: Tell categorical from numerical data questions
questions.stem: Maria collects data on the number of letters in each classmate's first name. What kind of data is this?
choices: Numerical, because the answers are names.
Categorical, because the answers are counts.
Categorical, because the answers are names.
Numerical, because the answers are counts.
questions.answer: Numerical, because the answers are counts.
questions.solution: The number of letters is a number (a count), so the data is numerical.

solve.answer: Numerical, because the answers are counts.
solve.work: Number of letters is a count, so numerical data because the answers are counts.

questions.skill: Tell categorical from numerical data questions
questions.stem: Here are five questions. (1) What is your favorite sport? (2) How many pets do you have? (3) How old are you? (4) What color is your backpack? (5) How many minutes does your walk to school take? How many of these questions give numerical data?
questions.solution: Questions 2, 3 and 5 have numbers as answers. Questions 1 and 4 have words as answers. So 3 questions give numerical data.

solve.work: (2) pets count, (3) age, (5) minutes are numerical; (1) sport and (4) colour are categorical. 3.

questions.skill: Read a line plot
questions.stem: A line plot shows how many pencils each of 10 students has. Each X stands for 1 student. There are 2 X marks above 3, 5 X marks above 4 and 3 X marks above 5. How many students have 4 pencils?
questions.solution: The number of X marks above 4 is the number of students with 4 pencils: 5 students.

questions.skill: Read a line plot
questions.stem: A line plot shows the number of letters in the first names of 15 students. Each X stands for 1 student. There are 4 X marks above 4, 6 X marks above 5, 2 X marks above 6 and 3 X marks above 7. Which number of letters is the most common?
questions.solution: The tallest stack of X marks is above 5 (6 marks), so 5 letters is the most common.

questions.skill: Show data in a frequency table
questions.stem: Ben asked 8 friends how many books they read last month. The answers were 2, 3, 3, 4, 3, 2, 5, 3. Ben makes a table with a row for each number of books. How many friends go in the row for 3 books?
questions.solution: Count the 3s in the list: 3, 3, 3, 3. There are 4.

solve.work: Answers 2,3,3,4,3,2,5,3: the 3s are at positions 2,3,5,8 = 4 friends.

questions.skill: Show data in a frequency table
questions.stem: Dee asked 6 children how many pets they have and got these answers: 1, 2, 2, 3, 2, 1. Which table shows her data correctly?
choices: 1 pet: 2 children, 2 pets: 2 children, 3 pets: 2 children.
1 pet: 3 children, 2 pets: 2 children, 3 pets: 1 child.
1 pet: 2 children, 2 pets: 3 children, 3 pets: 1 child.
1 pet: 1 child, 2 pets: 2 children, 3 pets: 3 children.
questions.answer: 1 pet: 2 children, 2 pets: 3 children, 3 pets: 1 child.
questions.solution: Count each answer: 1 appears 2 times, 2 appears 3 times, 3 appears 1 time. That makes 2 + 3 + 1 = 6 children.

solve.answer: 1 pet: 2 children, 2 pets: 3 children, 3 pets: 1 child.
solve.work: 1,2,2,3,2,1: 1 pet twice, 2 pets three times, 3 pets once.

questions.skill: Read bar graphs and choose a display
questions.stem: A bar graph shows votes for a class game. The bar for chess goes up to 9. The bar for cards goes up to 14. The bar for dominoes goes up to 6. How many more votes did cards get than chess?
questions.solution: Subtract: 14 - 9 = 5 more votes.

questions.skill: Show data on a line plot
questions.stem: Pia makes a line plot of the number of siblings that 9 students have. She puts one X above the number for each student. Three students have 0 siblings, 4 students have 1 sibling and the rest have 2 siblings. How many X marks go above 2?
questions.solution: 3 + 4 = 7 students have 0 or 1 sibling. The rest have 2: 9 - 7 = 2 X marks.

questions.skill: Answer questions from collected data
questions.stem: A team scored these numbers of goals in 5 games: 2, 4, 1, 3, 5. How many goals did the team score in all?

questions.skill: Tell categorical from numerical data questions
questions.stem: Which set of data is numerical?
choices: The number of siblings of 12 students
questions.answer: The number of siblings of 12 students
questions.solution: Number of siblings is a count, so its data is numerical. Fruits, eye colors and pets are categories.

solve.answer: The number of siblings of 12 students
solve.work: Number of siblings is a count (numerical); eye colours, fruits and pets are categories.

questions.skill: Tell categorical from numerical data questions
questions.stem: Mr. Fox asks his class: "How many glasses of water did you drink today?" Which statement is true?
choices: It is a categorical question, so a line plot can show the answers.
It is a numerical question, so the answers cannot be put in a graph.
It is a categorical question, so the answers cannot be put in a graph.
It is a numerical question, so a line plot can show the answers.
questions.answer: It is a numerical question, so a line plot can show the answers.
questions.solution: The answers are numbers (0, 1, 2, ...), so the question is numerical, and numerical data can be shown on a line plot.

solve.answer: It is a numerical question, so a line plot can show the answers.
solve.work: Answers are numbers, so numerical; numerical data can be shown on a line plot.

questions.skill: Read a line plot
questions.stem: A line plot shows the lengths in inches of 10 leaves. Each X stands for 1 leaf. There are 3 X marks above 2, 4 above 3, 2 above 4 and 1 above 5. How many leaves are longer than 3 inches?
questions.solution: Longer than 3 inches means the marks above 4 and 5: 2 + 1 = 3 leaves.

questions.skill: Read a line plot
questions.stem: A line plot shows the cups of juice that 12 children drank. Each X stands for 1 child. There is 1 X above 0, 3 above 1, 5 above 2, 2 above 3 and 1 above 4. How many children drank 2 or more cups?
questions.solution: Add the marks above 2, 3 and 4: 5 + 2 + 1 = 8 children.

questions.skill: Show data in a frequency table
questions.stem: A table shows how many pets some children have. 1 pet: 5 children. 2 pets: 7 children. 3 pets: 4 children. 4 pets: 2 children. How many children were asked?
questions.solution: Each child is in exactly one row, so add the rows: 5 + 7 + 4 + 2 = 18 children.

questions.skill: Show data in a frequency table
questions.stem: Lee recorded the number of points scored in 8 games: 4, 6, 5, 4, 6, 4, 7, 4. In his table, the row for 4 points is missing its number of games. The other rows are 5 points: 1 game, 6 points: 2 games and 7 points: 1 game. How many games go in the row for 4 points?
questions.solution: There are 8 games in all. The other rows hold 1 + 2 + 1 = 4 games, so the 4-point row has 8 - 4 = 4 games. (Counting the 4s in the list also gives 4.)

questions.skill: Read bar graphs and choose a display
questions.stem: A bar graph shows how many students chose each snack. The bar for nuts goes up to 7. The bar for fruit is twice as tall as the bar for nuts. How many students chose fruit?
questions.solution: Twice as tall means 2 times 7 = 14 students.

questions.skill: Show data on a line plot
questions.stem: Three students each have 2 pets. Which tells how to show these students on a line plot of the number of pets?
choices: Put 2 X marks above the number 3.
Put 3 X marks above the number 2.
Put 1 X mark above the number 6.
Put 6 X marks above the number 1.
questions.answer: Put 3 X marks above the number 2.
questions.solution: Each X stands for one student, and the number it sits above is the number of pets. Three students with 2 pets each means 3 X marks above 2.

solve.answer: Put 3 X marks above the number 2.
solve.work: Each student is one X above the number of pets, 2: 3 X marks above 2.

questions.skill: Show data on a line plot
questions.stem: Here are the heights in inches of 7 plants: 3, 4, 4, 5, 4, 3, 6. Ray makes a line plot with one X for each plant. How many X marks go above 4?
questions.solution: Count the plants that are 4 inches tall: 4, 4, 4. That is 3 X marks.

questions.skill: Answer questions from collected data
questions.stem: Six students each recorded how many books they read: 4, 6, 3, 6, 5, 6. How many more books did the student who read the most read than the student who read the fewest?
questions.solution: The most is 6 and the fewest is 3. 6 - 3 = 3 more books.

questions.skill: Tell categorical from numerical data questions
questions.stem: Four students each collect data from their classmates. Which student collects numerical data?
choices: Ana records the type of shoe each classmate is wearing.
Cleo records the color of each classmate's backpack.
Dan records which team each classmate cheers for.
Ben records how many steps each classmate takes to cross the room.
questions.answer: Ben records how many steps each classmate takes to cross the room.
questions.solution: Only the number of steps is a number. Shoe type, backpack color and favorite team are categories.

solve.answer: Ben records how many steps each classmate takes to cross the room.
solve.work: Number of steps is a count, numerical. Shoe type, team, colour are categorical.

questions.skill: Read a line plot
questions.stem: A line plot shows the number of library books in 15 backpacks. Each X stands for 1 backpack. There are 2 X marks above 1, 5 above 2, 6 above 3 and 2 above 4. How many library books are in all 15 backpacks together?
questions.solution: Multiply each number of books by its marks and add: 1 x 2 = 2, 2 x 5 = 10, 3 x 6 = 18, 4 x 2 = 8. 2 + 10 + 18 + 8 = 38 books.

questions.skill: Read a line plot
questions.stem: A line plot shows the minutes 11 students practiced piano. Each X stands for 1 student. There are 3 X marks above 10, 5 above 15, 2 above 20 and 1 above 30. What is the difference between the longest and the shortest practice time, in minutes?
questions.solution: The longest time is 30 minutes and the shortest is 10 minutes. 30 - 10 = 20 minutes.

questions.skill: Show data in a frequency table
questions.stem: Twelve students had these quiz scores: 7, 8, 9, 8, 10, 7, 8, 9, 8, 7, 10, 8. Which sentence about a frequency table of these scores is true?
questions.solution: Count each score: 7 appears 3 times, 8 appears 5 times, 9 appears 2 times, 10 appears 2 times (3 + 5 + 2 + 2 = 12). So 5 students scored 8.

questions.skill: Read bar graphs and choose a display
questions.stem: Which question has data that is best shown on a line plot?
choices: Which fruit did you eat for your snack today?
How many glasses of water did you drink?
Which sport do you like to play the most?
What is your favorite subject in school?
questions.answer: How many glasses of water did you drink?
questions.solution: A line plot puts X marks above numbers, so it suits numerical data. Only the first question has numbers as answers; the others have categories, which a bar graph shows better.

solve.answer: How many glasses of water did you drink?
solve.work: Glasses of water is numerical data, suited to a line plot; the others are categorical.

questions.skill: Read bar graphs and choose a display
questions.stem: A bar graph shows how many students chose each weekend activity. Movies: 13. Park: 9. Games: 15. Swimming: 11. Each student chose one activity. How many students were asked?
questions.solution: Add the four bars: 13 + 9 = 22, 22 + 15 = 37, 37 + 11 = 48 students.

questions.skill: Answer questions from collected data
questions.stem: A team scored these numbers of goals in 7 games: 3, 5, 2, 5, 4, 5, 1. Which statement is true?
choices: The most common number of goals is 3.
The total number of goals is 21.
The most goals minus the fewest goals is 3.
The most common number of goals is 5.
questions.answer: The most common number of goals is 5.
questions.solution: 5 appears 3 times, more than any other number. The total is 3 + 5 + 2 + 5 + 4 + 5 + 1 = 25, and the most minus the fewest is 5 - 1 = 4.

solve.answer: The most common number of goals is 5.
solve.work: 3,5,2,5,4,5,1: 5 appears 3 times (mode 5). Total = 25, not 21. Max-min = 5-1 = 4, not 3. Only "most common is 5" is true.

questions.skill: Answer questions from collected data
questions.stem: Maya recorded the number of laps that 11 runners ran: 4, 5, 5, 6, 4, 7, 5, 6, 5, 8, 7. How many runners ran more than 5 laps?
questions.solution: The numbers greater than 5 are 6, 7, 6, 8 and 7. That is 5 runners.

questions.skill: Answer questions from collected data
questions.stem: A survey asks 25 students how many pets they have. 8 students have 0 pets, 9 have 1 pet and 5 have 2 pets. The rest have 3 pets. How many pets do the 25 students have in all?
questions.solution: 8 + 9 + 5 = 22 students are in the first rows, so 25 - 22 = 3 students have 3 pets. Pets: 0 x 8 + 1 x 9 + 2 x 5 + 3 x 3 = 0 + 9 + 10 + 9 = 28.

questions.skill: Show data on a line plot
questions.stem: Cara asked 12 classmates how many brothers and sisters they have: 2, 3, 3, 4, 2, 3, 5, 3, 4, 3, 2, 4. She makes a line plot with one X for each classmate. How many more X marks go above 3 than above 2?
questions.solution: Count each number. The number 3 appears 5 times, so 5 X marks go above 3. The number 2 appears 3 times, so 3 X marks go above 2. The difference is $5 - 3 = 2$.

solve.work: Data 2,3,3,4,2,3,5,3,4,3,2,4. Count of 2: three. Count of 3: five. Difference 5 - 3 = 2.

questions.skill: Understand an angle as degrees
questions.stem: An angle is made of 40 one-degree angles fitted together with no gaps or overlaps. How many degrees is the angle?
questions.solution: Each one-degree angle is 1 degree. 40 of them make an angle of 40 degrees.

questions.skill: Degrees and turns of a circle
questions.stem: How many degrees is a right angle?
questions.solution: A right angle is a quarter of a full turn. A full turn is 360 degrees, and 360 / 4 = 90 degrees.

questions.skill: Measure an angle with a protractor
questions.stem: Mara puts a protractor on an angle. One ray lies on the 0 mark. The other ray passes through the 70 mark on the same scale. How many degrees is the angle?
questions.solution: When one ray is on 0, the mark the other ray crosses on that scale is the measure. The angle is 70 degrees.

solve.work: From 0 to 70 on the same scale: 70.

questions.skill: Classify angles as acute, right, obtuse or straight
questions.stem: Which angle is acute?
questions.solution: An acute angle is smaller than a right angle (90 degrees). Only 30 degrees is less than 90 degrees.

questions.skill: Find an unknown angle
questions.stem: A right angle is split into two angles. One of them is $30^\circ$. How many degrees is the other angle?
questions.solution: A right angle is 90 degrees. The two parts together make 90 degrees. 90 - 30 = 60 degrees.

questions.skill: Degrees and turns of a circle
questions.stem: Kai spins around in place for a half turn. How many degrees does he turn?
questions.solution: A full turn is 360 degrees. A half turn is half of that: 360 / 2 = 180 degrees.

questions.skill: Measure an angle with a protractor
questions.stem: Which tool is used to measure an angle in degrees?
questions.solution: A protractor has a scale marked in degrees. A ruler measures length, a thermometer measures temperature and a measuring cup measures amount of liquid.

questions.skill: Add angles to find a whole angle
questions.stem: Two angles sit side by side and share a ray. They make angle ABD. Angle ABC is $25^\circ$ and angle CBD is $40^\circ$. How many degrees is angle ABD?
questions.solution: Angle measures add when the angles sit side by side. 25 + 40 = 65 degrees.

questions.skill: Classify angles as acute, right, obtuse or straight
questions.stem: Which angle is obtuse?
questions.solution: An obtuse angle is bigger than a right angle (90 degrees) and smaller than a straight angle (180 degrees). Only 140 degrees fits.

questions.skill: Degrees and turns of a circle
questions.stem: The minute hand of a clock moves from the 12 to the 3. How many degrees does it turn?
questions.solution: From the 12 to the 3 is a quarter of the way around the clock. A quarter of 360 degrees is 90 degrees.

questions.skill: Add angles to find a whole angle
questions.stem: Ray BD is inside angle ABC. Angle ABD is $48^\circ$ and angle DBC is $37^\circ$. How many degrees is angle ABC?
questions.solution: Angle ABC is made of the two smaller angles. 48 + 37 = 85 degrees.

questions.skill: Find an unknown angle
questions.stem: Two angles together make a straight angle. One of them is $125^\circ$. How many degrees is the other angle?
questions.solution: A straight angle is 180 degrees. 180 - 125 = 55 degrees.

questions.skill: Measure an angle with a protractor
questions.stem: A protractor has two scales. Ray AB lies on the 0 of the right-hand scale, which counts up going left. Ray AC crosses 40 on the left-hand scale and 140 on the right-hand scale. How many degrees is angle BAC?
questions.solution: Use the scale that starts at 0 on the first ray, AB. That is the right-hand scale, and ray AC crosses it at 140. The angle is 140 degrees. The 40 is from the other scale.

solve.work: AB is on 0 of the right-hand scale, so read AC on that scale: 140. (40 is the other scale.)

questions.skill: Sketch an angle with a protractor
questions.stem: Eli wants to sketch a $110^\circ$ angle. He lines up the first ray with the 0 on the right-hand scale, which counts up going left. Which mark should the second ray go through?
questions.solution: The second ray must go through the mark on the same scale that starts at 0 on the first ray. That is 110 on the right-hand scale.

solve.work: First ray on 0 of the right-hand scale, so use that scale: the mark 110 on the right-hand scale.

questions.skill: Degrees and turns of a circle
questions.stem: The minute hand of a clock takes 60 minutes to turn all the way around, which is 360 degrees. How many degrees does it turn in 20 minutes?
questions.solution: In 1 minute it turns 360 / 60 = 6 degrees. In 20 minutes: 6 x 20 = 120 degrees. (20 minutes is one third of the way around.)

questions.skill: Understand an angle as degrees
questions.stem: Angle P has rays 3 centimeters long. Angle Q has rays 6 centimeters long. The two angles open the same amount. Angle P measures $40^\circ$. What does angle Q measure?
questions.solution: The measure of an angle tells how far open it is. It does not depend on how long the rays are drawn. Angle Q is also 40 degrees.

solve.work: Angle size does not depend on ray length: 40.

questions.skill: Find an unknown angle
questions.stem: Three angles meet at one point and fill the whole circle around it with no gaps. Two of them are $100^\circ$ and $120^\circ$. How many degrees is the third angle?
questions.solution: The angles around a point make 360 degrees. 100 + 120 = 220, and 360 - 220 = 140 degrees.

questions.skill: Classify angles as acute, right, obtuse or straight
questions.stem: Which angle is NOT acute?
questions.solution: An acute angle is less than 90 degrees. 15, 45 and 89 degrees are all less than 90 degrees. 91 degrees is more than 90 degrees, so it is not acute.

questions.skill: Degrees and turns of a circle
questions.stem: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices from the center. How many degrees is the angle of one slice at the center?
questions.solution: The slices fill a full turn of 360 degrees. 360 / 8 = 45 degrees.

questions.skill: Measure an angle with a protractor
questions.stem: An angle looks wider than the corner of a sheet of paper. Sam measures it with a protractor and reads 35 on one scale and 145 on the other scale. How many degrees is the angle?
questions.solution: The corner of a sheet of paper is 90 degrees, and this angle is wider, so it is more than 90 degrees. So the angle is 145 degrees, not 35.

solve.work: Wider than a paper corner means obtuse, so the reading is 145 (35 is the other scale).

questions.skill: Find an unknown angle
questions.stem: Ray BD is inside angle ABC. Angle ABC is $145^\circ$ and angle ABD is $63^\circ$. How many degrees is angle DBC?
questions.solution: Angle DBC is the part of angle ABC that is left over. 145 - 63 = 82 degrees.

questions.skill: Find an unknown angle
questions.stem: A straight angle is split into three angles. Two of them are $40^\circ$ and $75^\circ$. How many degrees is the third angle?
questions.solution: A straight angle is 180 degrees. 40 + 75 = 115, and 180 - 115 = 65 degrees.

questions.skill: Degrees and turns of a circle
questions.stem: At 5 o'clock the minute hand points to the 12 and the hour hand points to the 5. The 12 numbers are spaced equally around the full circle of 360 degrees. How many degrees is the angle between the hands that is smaller than a straight angle?
questions.solution: The distance between neighbouring numbers is 360 / 12 = 30 degrees. From the 12 to the 5 is 5 steps: 5 x 30 = 150 degrees.

solve.work: Each number gap is 360/12 = 30; from 12 to 5 is 5 gaps = 150, which is less than 180.

questions.skill: Degrees and turns of a circle
questions.stem: An angle cuts off one sixth of a circle. How many degrees is the angle?
questions.solution: The full circle is 360 degrees. One sixth of it is 360 / 6 = 60 degrees.

questions.skill: Add angles to find a whole angle
questions.stem: Which two angles can be put together to make a straight angle?
questions.solution: A straight angle is 180 degrees. 115 + 65 = 180. The other pairs add to 170, 190 and 170.

questions.skill: Find an unknown angle
questions.stem: A right angle is split into three angles. Two of them are $25^\circ$ and $38^\circ$. How many degrees is the third angle?
questions.solution: A right angle is 90 degrees. 25 + 38 = 63, and 90 - 63 = 27 degrees.

questions.skill: Understand an angle as degrees
questions.stem: An angle is made of 120 one-degree angles. What fraction of a full circle is it?
questions.solution: A full circle has 360 one-degree angles. The fraction is 120 / 360 = 1/3.

questions.skill: Measure an angle with a protractor
questions.stem: Sia measures angle BAC, but her protractor is shifted so that ray AB is not on the 0. Ray AB crosses the 20 mark and ray AC crosses the 85 mark, both on the same scale. How many degrees is angle BAC?
questions.solution: The angle is the gap between the two readings on the same scale. 85 - 20 = 65 degrees.

questions.skill: Sketch an angle with a protractor
questions.stem: Rae sketches a $125^\circ$ angle without a protractor. Which description fits best?
choices: Much narrower than a square corner
A bit wider than a square corner
questions.answer: A bit wider than a square corner
questions.solution: 125 degrees is more than a right angle (90 degrees) but less than a straight angle (180 degrees). So it is a bit wider than a square corner.

solve.answer: A bit wider than a square corner
solve.work: 125 is more than 90 but much less than 180: a bit wider than a square corner is the best fit.

questions.skill: Classify angles as acute, right, obtuse or straight
questions.stem: Ana puts two angles side by side so they share a ray. One is $47^\circ$ and the other is $58^\circ$. What kind of angle do they make together?
questions.solution: 47 + 58 = 105 degrees. That is more than 90 degrees and less than 180 degrees, so the angle is obtuse.

questions.skill: Identify lines, segments and rays
questions.stem: Which figure goes on forever in both directions and has no endpoints?
questions.solution: A line goes on forever in both directions, so it has no endpoints. A ray has one endpoint, a line segment has two, and a point is a single spot.

solve.work: A line extends forever both ways with no endpoints.

questions.skill: Endpoints of segments and rays
questions.stem: How many endpoints does a ray have?
questions.solution: A ray starts at one endpoint and goes on forever in one direction. It has 1 endpoint.

solve.work: A ray has one endpoint and extends forever in one direction.

questions.skill: Identify lines, segments and rays
questions.stem: Which figure is a straight path that starts at one point and stops at another point?
questions.solution: A line segment has two endpoints, so it starts and stops. A ray and a line go on forever in at least one direction.

solve.work: A straight path from one point to another is a line segment.

questions.skill: Classify angles as right, acute or obtuse
questions.stem: An angle makes a square corner, like the corner of a sheet of paper. What kind of angle is it?
questions.solution: An angle that makes a square corner is a right angle. An acute angle is smaller than a square corner and an obtuse angle is wider.

solve.work: A square corner is a right angle (90 degrees).

questions.skill: Parallel lines
questions.stem: Two lines lie flat on the same page. No matter how far they are extended, they never cross. What are the lines called?
questions.solution: Lines that stay the same distance apart and never meet are parallel lines.

solve.work: Lines in a plane that never meet are parallel.

questions.skill: Count right angles
questions.stem: A rectangle has square corners. How many right angles does a rectangle have?
questions.solution: A rectangle has 4 corners and every corner is a square corner, so it has 4 right angles.

solve.work: A rectangle has 4 square corners, so 4 right angles.

questions.skill: Perpendicular lines
questions.stem: Two lines cross each other and make square corners. What are these lines called?
questions.solution: Lines that cross to make square corners (right angles) are perpendicular lines.

solve.work: Lines crossing at square corners are perpendicular.

questions.skill: Classify angles as right, acute or obtuse
questions.stem: An angle is smaller than a square corner. What kind of angle is it?
questions.solution: An angle smaller than a square corner (a right angle) is an acute angle.

solve.work: Smaller than a right angle is acute.

questions.skill: Endpoints of segments and rays
questions.stem: Rosa draws 3 separate line segments. No two of them share an endpoint. How many endpoints do the 3 segments have in all?
questions.solution: Each line segment has 2 endpoints. 3 segments have 3 × 2 = 6 endpoints.

solve.work: Each segment has 2 endpoints, none shared: 3 x 2 = 6.

questions.skill: Identify lines, segments and rays
questions.stem: Which is the best model of a ray?
choices: The straight edge of a classroom ruler
The tiny dot left by a sharp pen tip
A road that goes on forever both ways
A flashlight beam shining into the sky
questions.answer: A flashlight beam shining into the sky
questions.solution: A flashlight beam starts at the flashlight (one endpoint) and goes on and on in one direction, like a ray. A ruler edge is a segment, a dot is a point, and a road going both ways forever is like a line.

solve.answer: A flashlight beam shining into the sky
solve.work: A flashlight beam starts at the flashlight and goes on in one direction: a ray. The two-way road is a line, the ruler edge a segment, the dot a point.

questions.skill: Name figures with letters
questions.stem: Points A and B are on a line. Which name describes the part of the line that starts at A, passes through B and goes on forever?
questions.solution: A ray is named with its endpoint first. This part starts at A and goes through B, so it is ray AB. Ray BA would start at B, and segment AB stops at B.

solve.work: Starts at A, through B, forever: ray AB (endpoint named first).

questions.skill: Angles: vertex and rays
questions.stem: An angle is made of two rays that share an endpoint. What is that shared endpoint called?
questions.solution: The point where the two rays of an angle meet is called the vertex.

solve.work: The common endpoint of the two rays of an angle is the vertex.

questions.skill: Parallel and perpendicular sides in shapes
questions.stem: A rectangle has 4 sides. How many pairs of its sides are parallel?
questions.solution: The top and bottom sides are parallel, and the left and right sides are parallel. That is 2 pairs.

solve.work: Opposite sides of a rectangle are parallel: 2 pairs.

questions.skill: Perpendicular lines
questions.stem: On a map, Oak Street runs exactly east to west. Pine Street runs exactly north to south. How are the two streets related?
questions.solution: East-west and north-south directions make a square corner where they meet, so the streets are perpendicular.

solve.work: East-west and north-south meet at right angles: perpendicular.

questions.skill: Classify angles as right, acute or obtuse
questions.stem: A clock’s hour hand and minute hand can form a right angle. Look at these times: 3:00, 6:00, 9:00 and 12:00. At how many of these times do the two hands form a right angle?
questions.solution: At 3:00 and at 9:00 the hands make a square corner. At 6:00 they make a straight line, and at 12:00 they point the same way. So the answer is 2.

solve.work: 3:00 and 9:00 form right angles; 6:00 is a straight angle; 12:00 hands overlap. 2 times.

questions.skill: Identify lines, segments and rays
questions.stem: Which statement about a ray is true?
choices: It has two endpoints and a length you can measure.
It has no endpoints and goes on forever both ways.
It has one endpoint and stops after a short length.
It has one endpoint and goes on forever in one direction.
questions.answer: It has one endpoint and goes on forever in one direction.
questions.solution: A ray starts at one endpoint and goes on forever in one direction. A segment has two endpoints, and a line has none.

solve.answer: It has one endpoint and goes on forever in one direction.
solve.work: A ray has one endpoint and goes on forever in one direction.

questions.skill: Parallel lines
questions.stem: Which statement about parallel lines is false?
choices: They cross at a square corner.
They stay the same distance apart.
They can be drawn on a flat page.
questions.answer: They cross at a square corner.
questions.solution: Parallel lines never meet, so they cannot cross at a square corner. Lines that cross at a square corner are perpendicular.

solve.answer: They cross at a square corner.
solve.work: Parallel lines never cross, so "They cross at a square corner" is false; the rest are true.

questions.skill: Parallel lines
questions.stem: Which pair is the best model of parallel lines?
choices: Two sticks crossed to make an X
The two long edges of a ruler
The hands of a clock at 3:00
The two edges that meet at a book corner
questions.answer: The two long edges of a ruler
questions.solution: The long edges of a ruler stay the same distance apart and never meet. The other pairs all meet at a point.

solve.answer: The two long edges of a ruler
solve.work: The two long edges of a ruler never meet and stay the same distance apart: parallel. Clock at 3:00 and book corner are perpendicular; X is intersecting.

questions.skill: Count right angles
questions.stem: Two perpendicular lines cross each other. They make 4 angles where they cross. How many of these angles are right angles?
questions.solution: Perpendicular lines make square corners where they cross, and all 4 angles around the crossing point are right angles.

questions.skill: Parallel and perpendicular sides in shapes
questions.stem: A regular hexagon has 6 sides. Each side is parallel to the side directly across from it. How many pairs of parallel sides does the hexagon have?
questions.solution: The 6 sides pair up with the sides across from them: 6 ÷ 2 = 3 pairs.

solve.work: 6 sides, each paired with its opposite: 6/2 = 3 pairs.

questions.skill: Identify lines, segments and rays
questions.stem: Sam says that segment AB and ray AB are the same figure. Ray AB starts at A and passes through B. Which statement best explains how they are different?
choices: Segment AB goes on forever past B, but ray AB stops at B.
Ray AB and segment AB both have two endpoints, A and B.
Ray AB goes on forever past B, but segment AB stops at B.
Ray AB starts at B and goes through A.
questions.answer: Ray AB goes on forever past B, but segment AB stops at B.
questions.solution: Segment AB has two endpoints, A and B, and stops at B. Ray AB has only the endpoint A and continues past B forever.

solve.answer: Ray AB goes on forever past B, but segment AB stops at B.
solve.work: The ray continues past B forever; the segment stops at B.

questions.skill: Classify angles as right, acute or obtuse
questions.stem: Angle P is smaller than a square corner. Angle Q is wider than a square corner but is not a straight line. Angle R is exactly a square corner. Which list names the angles P, Q and R in that order?
questions.solution: Smaller than a square corner is acute, wider than a square corner (but not straight) is obtuse, and exactly a square corner is right. So P, Q, R are acute, obtuse, right.

solve.work: P smaller than right: acute; Q wider but not straight: obtuse; R exactly right: right.

questions.skill: Perpendicular lines
questions.stem: Lines m and n are different lines. Each crosses line p at a square corner. All three lines lie flat on the same page. How are lines m and n related?
questions.solution: Two different lines that are both perpendicular to the same line, on the same flat page, point the same way and never meet. They are parallel.

solve.work: Two lines in a plane both perpendicular to the same line are parallel.

questions.skill: Parallel and perpendicular sides in shapes
questions.stem: The corners of a rectangle are named A, B, C and D in order around the rectangle. Which segment is parallel to segment AB?
questions.solution: In order around the rectangle, AB and CD are opposite sides, so they are parallel. BC and AD meet AB at square corners, and AC goes across the rectangle from one corner to the opposite corner.

solve.work: In rectangle ABCD, AB is opposite CD, so CD is parallel to AB. AD and BC are perpendicular to AB; AC is a diagonal.

questions.skill: Parallel and perpendicular sides in shapes
questions.stem: The capital letter E is drawn with 4 line segments: 1 tall vertical segment and 3 short horizontal segments, each joined to the vertical one at a square corner. How many pairs of parallel segments are in the letter?
questions.solution: Only the 3 horizontal segments are parallel to each other. Pairs: top and middle, top and bottom, middle and bottom. That is 3 pairs.

solve.work: The 3 horizontal segments are parallel to each other: pairs = 3 (top-middle, top-bottom, middle-bottom). The vertical one is perpendicular to each.

questions.skill: Name figures with letters
questions.stem: Points P, Q and R lie on one straight line, with Q between P and R. Ray QP and ray QR both start at Q. Together, which figure do the two rays make?
questions.solution: Ray QP goes from Q through P forever, and ray QR goes from Q through R forever, in the opposite direction. Together they make the whole line, with no endpoints.

solve.work: Two opposite rays from Q along the same line together form the whole line PR.

questions.skill: Classify angles as right, acute or obtuse
questions.stem: Ava says, “Every acute angle is smaller than every right angle.” Which statement is correct?
choices: Ava is wrong, because some acute angles are wider than a square corner.
Ava is wrong, because a right angle is smaller than an acute angle.
Ava is wrong, because an acute angle is the same size as a right angle.
Ava is right, because an acute angle is smaller than a square corner.
questions.answer: Ava is right, because an acute angle is smaller than a square corner.
questions.solution: An acute angle is any angle smaller than a square corner, and a right angle is a square corner. So every acute angle is smaller than every right angle.

solve.answer: Ava is right, because an acute angle is smaller than a square corner.
solve.work: Every acute angle is less than 90 degrees and every right angle is exactly 90, so Ava is right.

questions.skill: Count right angles
questions.stem: Two parallel lines are both crossed by a third line that is perpendicular to them. At each of the 2 crossings, 4 angles are made. How many of these angles, in all, are right angles?
questions.solution: The third line crosses each parallel line at a square corner, so all 4 angles at each crossing are right angles. 2 crossings × 4 angles = 8.

solve.work: Each crossing is perpendicular, giving 4 right angles; 2 crossings: 8.

questions.skill: Name figures with letters
questions.stem: Four points A, B, C and D lie on one straight line. How many different line segments can be named that have two of these points as their endpoints?
questions.solution: Segments: AB, AC, AD, BC, BD and CD. That is 6 segments.

solve.work: Choose 2 of 4 points: AB, AC, AD, BC, BD, CD = 6.

questions.skill: Classify a triangle by its angles
questions.stem: A triangle has one angle that measures $90^\circ$. What kind of triangle is it?
questions.solution: A triangle with a $90^\circ$ angle (a square corner) is a right triangle. An acute triangle has only angles smaller than $90^\circ$, and an obtuse triangle has one angle larger than $90^\circ$.

solve.work: A 90 degree angle makes it a right triangle.

questions.skill: Classify a triangle by its sides
questions.stem: A scalene triangle has no sides of equal length. Which triangle is scalene?
choices: sides of 4 cm, 5 cm and 6 cm
sides of 6 cm, 6 cm and 6 cm
sides of 5 cm, 5 cm and 8 cm
sides of 7 cm, 7 cm and 3 cm
questions.answer: sides of 4 cm, 5 cm and 6 cm
questions.solution: The sides 4 cm, 5 cm and 6 cm are all different, so the triangle is scalene. The other triangles each have at least two sides of equal length.

solve.answer: sides of 4 cm, 5 cm and 6 cm

questions.skill: Name a quadrilateral from its sides and angles
questions.stem: A quadrilateral has exactly one pair of parallel sides. What is it called?
questions.solution: A trapezoid has exactly one pair of parallel sides. Rectangles, rhombuses and parallelograms all have two pairs of parallel sides.

solve.work: Exactly one pair of parallel sides: trapezoid.

questions.skill: Use the properties of a shape to find a length or count
questions.stem: How many right angles does a rectangle have?
questions.solution: Every corner of a rectangle is a square corner, which is a right angle. A rectangle has 4 corners, so it has 4 right angles.

questions.skill: Classify a triangle by its angles
questions.stem: A triangle has angles of $35^\circ$, $45^\circ$ and $100^\circ$. What kind of triangle is it?
questions.solution: The angle of $100^\circ$ is larger than a right angle ($90^\circ$), so the triangle has an obtuse angle. It is an obtuse triangle.

solve.work: 100 degrees is obtuse, so an obtuse triangle (angles sum to 180).

questions.skill: Classify a triangle by its sides
questions.stem: An equilateral triangle has a perimeter of 18 cm. How many centimeters long is each side?
questions.solution: An equilateral triangle has 3 sides of equal length. Each side is $18 \div 3 = 6$ cm.

questions.skill: Parallel and perpendicular lines and sides
questions.stem: Two lines cross and make a right angle. What word describes these lines?
questions.solution: Lines that meet to make a right angle (a square corner) are perpendicular. Parallel lines never meet.

solve.work: Lines meeting at a right angle are perpendicular.

questions.skill: Parallel and perpendicular lines and sides
questions.stem: How many pairs of parallel sides does a parallelogram have?
questions.solution: A parallelogram has two pairs of sides that are parallel: the top and bottom, and the left and right sides. So it has 2 pairs.

solve.work: A parallelogram has 2 pairs of parallel sides.

questions.skill: Classify a triangle by its sides
questions.stem: Which triangle is equilateral?
choices: sides of 7 cm, 7 cm and 3 cm
sides of 7 cm, 5 cm and 3 cm
sides of 7 cm, 8 cm and 9 cm
sides of 7 cm, 7 cm and 7 cm
questions.answer: sides of 7 cm, 7 cm and 7 cm
questions.solution: An equilateral triangle has all three sides the same length. Only the triangle with sides of 7 cm, 7 cm and 7 cm has this.

solve.answer: sides of 7 cm, 7 cm and 7 cm

questions.skill: Classify a triangle by its sides
questions.stem: A triangle has sides that measure 7 cm, 7 cm and 3 cm. What is this triangle called, by its sides?
questions.solution: Two of its sides are equal in length (7 cm and 7 cm) and the third is different, so it is isosceles. An equilateral triangle has three equal sides and a scalene triangle has none.

solve.work: Two sides equal (7 and 7), so isosceles. Not equilateral (3 differs), not scalene; right is an angle name.

questions.skill: Classify a triangle by its angles
questions.stem: Four triangles have these angles. Triangle A: $30^\circ$, $60^\circ$, $90^\circ$. Triangle B: $50^\circ$, $60^\circ$, $70^\circ$. Triangle C: $25^\circ$, $25^\circ$, $130^\circ$. Triangle D: $45^\circ$, $45^\circ$, $90^\circ$. How many of the triangles are right triangles?
questions.solution: A right triangle has a $90^\circ$ angle. Triangles A and D each have one, Triangle B has only acute angles, and Triangle C has an obtuse angle. So 2 are right triangles.

solve.work: Right triangles: A (90) and D (90). B acute, C obtuse. 2.

questions.skill: Name a quadrilateral from its sides and angles
questions.stem: A quadrilateral has 4 right angles and its opposite sides are equal in length. Two sides that meet at a corner measure 8 cm and 3 cm. What is the most specific name for this shape?
questions.solution: All four angles are right angles and the neighboring sides are different lengths, so it is a rectangle. A square and a rhombus would need all four sides equal, and 8 cm is not 3 cm.

solve.work: 4 right angles, opposite sides equal, adjacent sides 8 and 3 differ: rectangle, not square.

questions.skill: Name a quadrilateral from its sides and angles
questions.stem: A quadrilateral has 4 sides of equal length. Its opposite sides are parallel, and it has no right angles. What is the most specific name for this shape?
questions.solution: A shape with 4 equal sides and opposite sides parallel is a rhombus. It has no right angles, so it is not a square or a rectangle.

solve.work: 4 equal sides, opposite sides parallel, no right angles: rhombus.

questions.skill: Parallel and perpendicular lines and sides
questions.stem: Which statement about every rectangle is true?
choices: All four of its sides are equal in length
It has exactly one pair of parallel sides
questions.solution: A rectangle has four square corners, so it has four right angles. Its opposite sides are parallel (two pairs), and its sides need not all be equal.

solve.work: Every rectangle has four right angles; the others are false in general.

questions.skill: Classify a triangle by its angles
questions.stem: Which set of angle measures belongs to an acute triangle?
questions.solution: An acute triangle has all three angles smaller than $90^\circ$. Only $60^\circ$, $60^\circ$, $60^\circ$ qualifies; the others have a right angle or an obtuse angle.

solve.work: 60,60,60 all under 90: acute. Others have 90, 100 or 120.

questions.skill: Classify a triangle by its sides
questions.stem: Six triangles have these side lengths in centimeters. A: 5, 5, 5. B: 6, 6, 9. C: 7, 8, 9. D: 4, 6, 8. E: 3, 4, 5. F: 10, 10, 4. How many of the triangles are scalene?
questions.solution: A scalene triangle has no two sides equal. Triangles C, D and E have three different side lengths. A has all equal sides and B and F each have two equal sides. So 3 are scalene.

solve.work: Scalene: C (7,8,9), D (4,6,8), E (3,4,5). A equilateral, B and F isosceles. 3.

questions.skill: Sort or count shapes by a property
questions.stem: Here are five shapes: a square; a trapezoid with exactly one pair of parallel sides; a triangle; a rhombus; a four-sided shape with no parallel sides. How many of these shapes have at least one pair of parallel sides?
questions.solution: The square, the trapezoid and the rhombus each have at least one pair of parallel sides. A triangle has no parallel sides, and neither does the last shape. So the answer is 3.

solve.work: Square, trapezoid, rhombus have parallel sides; triangle and the no-parallel quad do not. 3.

questions.skill: Use the properties of a shape to find a length or count
questions.stem: A square has a perimeter of 28 cm. How many centimeters long is each side?
questions.solution: A square has 4 sides of equal length. Each side is $28 \div 4 = 7$ cm.

questions.skill: Name a quadrilateral from its sides and angles
questions.stem: Which shape always has four right angles?
questions.solution: A rectangle always has four right angles. A rhombus, a trapezoid or a parallelogram can be drawn with no right angles at all.

solve.work: A rectangle always has four right angles.

questions.skill: Sort quadrilaterals by parallel sides
questions.stem: Here are five shapes: a rectangle; a square; a rhombus; a trapezoid with exactly one pair of parallel sides; a four-sided shape with no parallel sides. How many of these shapes have two pairs of parallel sides?
questions.solution: A rectangle, a square and a rhombus each have both pairs of opposite sides parallel. The trapezoid has only one pair of parallel sides and the last shape has none. So 3 of the shapes have two pairs of parallel sides.
